author: colinmollenhour
body:
## Summary

Implements Wishlist [#18](https://github.com/ShipStream/bloodraven/blob/main/WISHLIST.md): a `kubectl bloodraven` plugin that wraps the operator's annotation grammars and on-demand CR shapes so day-2 work no longer requires hand-crafted `kubectl annotate` / `kubectl apply` incantations.

The plugin only writes API objects the operator already understands — it never talks to MySQL, never bypasses the cooldown, and never holds state of its own. Operator-side validation (cooldown, role, divergent GTID prefix match, profile existence) is preserved exactly as today; the plugin adds **pre-flight** checks so typos surface immediately instead of being deferred to a `Failed{UnknownSite}` event on a freshly-created CR.

### Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `status [group]` | One-shot health: active site, per-site state/replication/recovery, planned-failover phase, restore, backup schedules, PITR window, conditions. Supports `table` / `wide` / `json` / `yaml` and `--all-namespaces`. |
| `promote <group> <site>` | Applies the documented `planned-failover` annotation grammar with optional `--max-lag-wait` / `--drain-timeout`. `--wait` streams phase transitions and exits non-zero on `Failed`. |
| `reclone <group> <site>` | Annotates `reclone-site`; auto-pulls the first 12 chars of `status.sites[].divergentGtid` so the safety interlock is satisfied without copy-pasting. `--gtid-prefix` overrides. |
| `backup <group> --profile <name>` | Creates a `MysqlBackup` mirroring the controller `trigger-backup` label set and naming convention. Optional `--source-site`, `--wait`. |
| `verify-backup <group> --profile <name>` | Creates a `MysqlBackupVerification`, inheriting `VerificationSpec` defaults (PITR / sanity-check) from the named profile so manual runs match scheduled ones. Optional `--backup`, `--wait`. |
| `version`, `help` | Plugin metadata and root help. |

### Build & install

```bash
make build-kubectl-plugin                                   # bin/kubectl-bloodraven
make build-kubectl-plugin KUBECTL_PLUGIN_VERSION=v0.2.0      # stamp version
make install-kubectl-plugin                                  # drop onto $PATH
```

### Operational impact

- **No CRD / RBAC changes.** The plugin runs with the caller's existing kubeconfig and RBAC.
- **No operator behavior changes.** The annotations / CR shapes the plugin writes are already supported in `main`.
- **Doc additions.** New page `docs/docs/kubectl-plugin.mdx` wired into the Operations sidebar; `docs/docs/operations.mdx` gets a cross-link tip. `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, and `WISHLIST.md` updated to mention the new binary and Make targets.

- [x] `make generate && make manifests` — no drift
- [x] `make vet`
- [x] `make lint` (golangci-lint)
- [x] `make test` (unit + component) — all green

- [x] `make build` + `make build-kubectl-plugin` — both produce binaries cleanly
- [x] Spot-check `kubectl bloodraven help` / `<cmd> --help` / `version` / unknown-command paths

## Description

This PR adds two related S3 storage improvements:

**1. S3 Key Prefix (`S3_KEY_PREFIX`)** — An optional environment variable that prepends a configurable prefix to all S3 object keys, allowing multiple Kaneo environments (e.g. `staging/`, `prod/kaneo/`) to share a single S3 bucket without key collisions. Trailing slashes are normalised automatically.

**2. Automatic S3 Asset Cleanup** — Previously, removing an image from a task description or comment only removed the reference in the editor — the actual S3 object remained as an orphan, accumulating storage costs. This PR adds automatic cleanup via a `deleteS3Object()` function and a `cleanup-assets` module that diffs old vs new content, identifies removed asset references, and deletes them from both S3 and the database. author: frhino
body:
## Problem

Node.js DEP0190 fires when `spawn()`/`execFileSync()` are called with `shell: true` and arguments passed as a separate array. On Windows, the args array is unsafely concatenated into the shell command string — Node.js rightfully warns about this.

This warning appears on every pi startup (visible as `[mcp-bridge] (node:XXXX) [DEP0190] DeprecationWarning` in the terminal).

## Root Cause

Three call sites in the source use the args-array form with `shell: true` on Windows:

1. `runtime.ts` — `runnableExists()`: `execFileSync(cmd, ["--version"], { shell: isWindows })`
2. `runtime.ts` — `getVersion()`: `execFileSync(cmd, args, { shell: process.platform === "win32" })`
3. `executor.ts` — `#spawn()`: `spawn(spawnCmd, spawnArgs, { shell: needsShell })` when `needsShell` is true (`tsx`/`ts-node`/`elixir`/`bun` on Windows)

## Fix

When shell is needed on Windows, collapse the command and arguments into a single string before passing to the child_process function. Leave the shell-free code path (POSIX) unchanged.

- **`runtime.ts`**: split into `execSync(cmdString)` on Windows vs `execFileSync(cmd, args)` without `shell` on POSIX
- **`executor.ts`**: when `needsShell` is true, join `spawnCmd + spawnArgs` into a single string, pass empty args array; otherwise keep the args-array form with `shell: false`

## Testing

Ran the original (pre-fix) bundle and the fixed bundle through the same MCP handshake + `ctx_execute` tool call:

| Bundle | stderr | Result |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Original | 264 bytes, contains `[DEP0190]` | ❌ |
| Fixed | 0 bytes | ✅ |

author: juampii01
body:
## Resumen

Milestone 3/4 — extiende el View-As (client-side) para incluir simulación de **departamento** y **usuario específico**, además del rol que ya estaba en milestone 2. Sigue siendo client-side; el server-side enforcement viene en milestone 4.

## Qué cambia

Antes: developer podía elegir un **rol** simulado.

Ahora: developer puede simular **3 ejes** (combinables):
- **Rol** (ya existía)
- **Departamento** — útil para ver tasks/inicio como si fueras de un depto específico
- **Usuario específico** — picker con search en /admin/team; al elegir, hereda rol + dept del user en un solo click

## Drawer rediseñado

El popover del top-bar pasa de 220px a 340px con 4 secciones claras:

1. **Rol** — los 5 botones (developer real / super_admin / admin / user / viewer).
2. **Departamento** — aparece solo cuando el rol simulado es user/viewer (un super_admin no necesita scoping). Lista departamentos desde el cache + "Todos".
3. **Usuario específico** — input search + lista filtrable de los 20 members. Click setea rol + dept + email atómicamente.
4. **"Volver a Developer (real)"** — botón ámbar sticky abajo cuando hay simulación.

## Banner inteligente

El texto del banner refleja qué se simula:
- `viewAsUser` → "Viendo como **Ana García** *(Empleado · IA)*"
- `viewAsRole + dept` → "Viendo como **Admin de Marketing**"
- Solo rol → "Viendo como **Empleado**"
- Solo dept → "Filtrado al depto **Anuncios**"

## Aplicación en vistas

| Vista | Qué hace |
|---|---|
| [tasks-view](components/views/tasks-view.tsx) | Filtro extra por `simulatedDeptId`; "mine" usa email del user simulado; chip "Solo [Depto] (simulación)" en toolbar |
| [inicio-view](components/views/inicio-view.tsx) | Card del depto simulado con ring ámbar; las otras dimadas a 40% |
| [team-view](components/views/team-view.tsx) | MemberCard del user simulado con ring ámbar + shadow |
| [top-bar](components/layout/top-bar.tsx) | Avatar + nombre del user simulado; gradient ámbar en el círculo; línea pequeña "↳ Simulando · Real: [email]" en el dropdown |

## Archivos

**Nuevos**
- [hooks/use-effective-identity.ts](hooks/use-effective-identity.ts) — devuelve `{role, departmentId, userId, isSimulating}`. `useEffectiveRole` queda como wrapper backward-compat.

**Modificados (significativamente)**
- [lib/contexts/view-as-context.tsx](lib/contexts/view-as-context.tsx) — 2 nuevos estados + caches + 4 nuevos setters
- [components/layout/view-as-dropdown.tsx](components/layout/view-as-dropdown.tsx) — drawer rebuild
- [components/layout/view-as-banner.tsx](components/layout/view-as-banner.tsx) — texto adaptativo
- [components/views/tasks-view.tsx](components/views/tasks-view.tsx) — filtro extra + email efectivo
- [components/views/inicio-view.tsx](components/views/inicio-view.tsx) — highlight/dim de cards
- [components/views/team-view.tsx](components/views/team-view.tsx) — highlight de MemberCard
- [components/layout/top-bar.tsx](components/layout/top-bar.tsx) — avatar + nombre simulados

## Decisiones tomadas

1. **Caches en el provider** (members + departments): el dropdown necesita la lista para el picker, y el banner necesita resolver nombres a partir de IDs. Centralizar evita refetches duplicados.
2. **`setViewAsUserId` busca en el cache** (no fetch async): per spec pedía auto-load, lo implementé buscando en el cache de members ya cargado. Si el id no está en cache (caso raro), es no-op. Más simple y sin race conditions.
3. **`setViewAsUser` setea cascade**: al elegir un usuario, automáticamente actualiza rol + dept + cache. Si después tocás `setViewAsRole` manualmente, NO se limpia el viewAsUser (per spec — la inconsistencia es OK porque es visible al developer).
4. **Filtro de dept aditivo** (no override del filterDepartment): si tenés un filterDepartment en la UI Y un simulatedDeptId, la task tiene que cumplir AMBOS. Si no coinciden, ves lista vacía (informativo).
5. **Avatar amber cuando se simula user**: para que sea obvio visualmente. Badge del rol mantiene el real para no perder identidad.
6. **Dept picker solo aparece si rol simulado es user/viewer**: per spec — un super_admin/admin no necesita estar scopeado a un depto. Si el developer quiere simular admin-de-X-depto, primero pone user y después el depto (aunque el typing real probablemente sea super_admin sin dept asignado).

## Limitaciones (vienen en milestone 4)

- **El server sigue devolviendo todas las tasks** porque ignora viewAs. El filtro es 100% client-side.
- **Si el user simulado tiene un dept** que el developer real no podría ver, la vista igual lo muestra (lo cual es esperado — developer ve todo, simular solo capa visual).
- **Acciones de escritura** (PATCH a un member, DELETE de un dept, etc.) siguen funcionando aunque la UI las oculte — porque el server enforce con rol real. Milestone 4 va a sumar opt-in server-side.

## Validación

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: pasa (exit 0).
- `pnpm lint`: 40 problemas (3 errors, 37 warnings) — **mismo baseline que milestone 2**, sin nuevos.
- Preview: `/inicio` compila y responde 200, sin errors en server logs.

## Testing manual sugerido

Después de mergear y `pnpm seed:demo`:

1. Login como `juampiacosta158@gmail.com` (developer).
2. Click 👁 → "Ana García" (empleada IA):
   - Banner: "Viendo como Ana García (Empleado · IA)"
   - Avatar top-bar: gradient amber + iniciales "AG"
   - Sidebar: sin Equipo ni Configuración (gating de user)
   - `/admin/tasks`: chip "Solo IA (simulación)" + lista filtrada al dept
   - `/inicio`: card "IA" destacada, las otras dimadas
   - `/admin/team`: el card de Ana con ring amber
3. Refresh → simulación persiste.
4. "Volver a Developer" → todo vuelve.
5. Como user real (no developer): nada de esto se ve.

author: jeremyjpj0916
body:
## Summary

Functional-test shards were each spending ~30 min, three avoidable causes:

1. **Each of 6 shards rebuilt the gateway binary** independently.
2. **The shard step looped `cargo test` once per filter line** (7-13 invocations per shard), paying cargo's fingerprint-check + libtest startup (~3-5s) every iteration → 30-60s of pure overhead per shard.
3. **libtest's shared-process scheduler** wasn't well-suited to this E2E suite — port/process contention compounds when many tests share one binary process.

This PR addresses all three:

- New `build-gateway-binary` job compiles `ferrum-edge` once and uploads the debug binary as an artifact. Each `test-functional` matrix entry downloads it instead of running its own `cargo build --bin ferrum-edge`.
- The per-filter `cargo test` loop collapses into one `cargo nextest run` invocation per shard, with all filters passed as positional argv (nextest treats them as substring filters OR'd together — identical selection semantics).
- `cargo-nextest` replaces `cargo test`. Its process-per-test model isolates port/process contention and ships built-in per-test slow/retry handling. `--run-ignored=all` mirrors libtest's `--include-ignored`; the two stress tests (`test_scale_perf_30k_proxies`, `test_load_stress_10k_proxies`) move from `--skip` flags into a nextest filter expression.

## Harness change

To make the build-sharing safe with nextest's one-process-per-test model, `tests/common/gateway_harness.rs::ensure_gateway_built()` gains a `FERRUM_SKIP_GATEWAY_BUILD` env var. When set, it just verifies `./target/debug/ferrum-edge` (or `release/`) exists and skips the cargo invocation. Without this, every test process would re-invoke `cargo build --bin ferrum-edge` on its first call — a no-op build, but ~200ms × N tests of fingerprint overhead per shard.

Local behavior is unchanged — the env var is only set in CI.

## Test plan

- [ ] Functional shards complete in under their previous wall-clock time
- [ ] Per-shard summary table still appears in GitHub job summary
- [ ] `build-gateway-binary` failure surfaces clearly in the test summary (now listed in `needs`)
- [ ] `cargo test --test functional_tests <filter>` still works locally (unchanged behavior without the env var)
- [ ] `FERRUM_SKIP_GATEWAY_BUILD=1 cargo test --test functional_tests <filter>` works locally when a binary is present in `target/debug/`
- [ ] Stress tests (`test_scale_perf_30k_proxies`, `test_load_stress_10k_proxies`) remain skipped in CI

author: medelman17
body:
## Summary

- Partially fixes #311 — addresses sub-bugs 3 (`, fn. 3` California footnote variant) and 4 (neutral paragraph pincites)
- Sub-bugs 1 (page-range in citation core) and 2 (CSM `pp.` multi-page list) are intentionally deferred to separate PRs
- 8 new tests; 178 net source/test lines; 0 regressions

## Sub-bugs fixed

### Sub-bug 3 — California `, fn. 3` footnote variant

`Smith v. Jones, 45 Cal.3d 744, 768, fn. 3` previously captured `pincite: 768` but dropped the footnote. The canonical `768 n.3` form already captured the footnote — only the California-Style-Manual variant (comma instead of whitespace separator, `fn.` instead of `n.`) was missed.

Extended both:
- `LOOKAHEAD_PINCITE_REGEX` (case-cite lookahead in `extractCase.ts`)
- `PINCITE_PARSE_REGEX` (structured pincite parser in `pincite.ts`)

Footnote-suffix separator now accepts `\s+` OR `,\s+`; alternation includes `fn` / `fns` alongside `n` / `nn` / `note`.

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `45 Cal.3d 744, 768, fn. 3` | `pincite: 768`, no footnote | + `footnote: 3` |
| `45 Cal.3d 744, 768, fns. 3-5` | `pincite: 768`, no range | + `footnote: 3, footnoteEnd: 5` |
| `45 Cal.3d 744, 768 n.3` (canonical) | unchanged | unchanged |

### Sub-bug 4 — neutral-cite paragraph pincites

`State v. Flores, 2015-NMCA-072, ¶ 2` previously captured the neutral cite but `pincite` and `pinciteInfo` were both undefined. State appellate practice universally uses paragraph numbering on neutral cites; missing them was a recall floor.

Extended `NEUTRAL_PINCITE_LOOKAHEAD` in `extractNeutral.ts` to accept the paragraph alternatives `¶¶? \d+(-\d+)?` / `paras?\.? \d+(-\d+)?` already used by the case-cite lookahead (#204). Added a fallback in the extractor: `pincite = pinciteInfo?.page ?? pinciteInfo?.paragraph` so the top-level numeric `pincite` field reflects the paragraph when no page is available.

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `2015-NMCA-072, ¶ 2` | `pincite: undefined`, no info | `pincite: 2`, `pinciteInfo: { paragraph: 2 }` |
| `2015-NMCA-072, ¶¶ 14-16` | undefined | `pincite: 14`, range with `endParagraph: 16` |
| `2020 WL 123456, at *3` (regression) | unchanged | unchanged |

## Intentionally deferred (separate follow-up PRs)

- **Sub-bug 1 — page ranges in citation core** (`109 N.E. 875-877`). State-reporter tokenizer requires single digit run for the page; `875-877` overflows. Needs tokenizer change + downstream range parsing. Larger, riskier.
- **Sub-bug 2 — CSM `pp. 238, 233` multi-page list**. Existing `ADDITIONAL_PINCITE_REGEX` (#247) doesn't fire on `pp.`-prefixed short-form path. Needs short-form extraction wiring.

## Files changed

- `src/extract/extractCase.ts` — `LOOKAHEAD_PINCITE_REGEX` footnote-suffix extension
- `src/extract/pincite.ts` — `PINCITE_PARSE_REGEX` matching extension
- `src/extract/extractNeutral.ts` — `NEUTRAL_PINCITE_LOOKAHEAD` paragraph alternatives + paragraph fallback
- `tests/extract/pincite.test.ts` — 2 unit tests
- `tests/extract/extractCase.test.ts` — 3 case-cite integration tests
- `tests/extract/extractNeutralHyphenated.test.ts` — 3 neutral-cite tests
- `.changeset/issue-311-pincite-variants.md`

## Test plan

- [x] 2 unit tests for the new pincite parser shapes
- [x] 3 case-cite integration tests for `, fn. 3` (+ multi-fn range + regression)
- [x] 3 neutral-cite tests for `¶` paragraph pincites (+ range + database-cite regression)
- [x] Full suite — 2456/2465 pass, 0 regressions
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean

author: scopsy
body: ## Summary Adds a top-level `.npmrc` to set pnpm's [`minimum-release-age`](https://pnpm.io/settings#minimumreleaseage) to **3 days (4320 minutes)**. ``` minimum-release-age=4320 ``` ## Why This is a supply-chain hardening measure. With `minimum-release-age` set, pnpm will refuse to install package versions that have been published less than the configured age ago, mitigating risk from compromised or malicious package releases that are typically caught and yanked within the first few days. ## Notes - The unit for `minimum-release-age` is **minutes**: `3 * 24 * 60 = 4320`. - This is a pnpm-only setting; npm ignores it. The repo currently uses npm, but the setting is harmless to npm-based workflows and will take effect for any pnpm install (local, CI, or future migration). - No code or dependency changes; only a single new config file. [Slack Thread](https://novu.slack.com/archives/D0919LNRWE7/p1778560010098619?thread_ts=1778560010.098619&cid=D0919LNRWE7)

I have added 5 specialized DevOps scripts to the repository, covering Kubernetes, GitHub, AWS, Docker, and general system utilities. 

- **Kubernetes**: `k8s_find_unused_pvcs.sh` identifies orphaned PVCs to help with cost and resource management.
- **GitHub**: `gh_delete_old_workflow_runs.sh` automates the cleanup of Actions history, including GNU date checks and pagination awareness.
- **General**: `backup_dir.sh` provides a reliable directory backup solution with retention logic that safely handles spaces in filenames.
- **AWS**: `aws_ec2_inventory.sh` offers a quick command-line overview of EC2 instances using JMESPath queries.
- **Docker**: `docker_show_image_layers.sh` helps developers optimize their images by displaying detailed layer information.

All scripts include `usage()` functions, tool presence verification, and follow the repository's standard of using `set -euo pipefail`. Relevant `README.md` files have been updated with descriptions and usage examples for the new tools.

author: sandgraal
body:
## Summary

Phase 4.5 backend. Compass now projects a per-account daily balance trajectory **90 days forward**, combining four event streams:

- **Subscriptions** (from the existing `auditSubscriptions` audit) → recurring outflows
- **Recurring income** detected from positive-amount txn cadence (biweekly / weekly / monthly payroll) → inflows
- **Debt minimums** on a per-account `paymentDayOfMonth` → monthly outflows
- **Calendar bills** filtered by finance keywords (`rent`, `mortgage`, `utilities`, etc.) → one-shot outflows

User overrides (skip / shift / override) live in a new `forecast_overrides` table and mutate the auto stream before projection. Low-cash detection flags the first date each account dips below a configurable threshold (default `$500`).

## What this does NOT do (deferred)

- **No UI yet.** The Forecast tab (Recharts trajectory + per-event popover with Skip/Shift/Override + low-cash banner) is a separate `ui-polish` PR. Recharts isn't in the dep tree yet — that PR will add it.
- **No probabilistic forecasting** (Monte Carlo over historical variance). Single-line projection only, per the design doc.
- **No "groceries running 15% hot, project that forward" YTD-pace re-forecast.** v2.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` — only pre-existing `electron-updater` types warning
- [x] `npm run check` — only pre-existing warnings, no new errors
- [x] `npm test` — **261/261 green**, including 26 new tests in `finance-forecast.test.ts`:
  - `localDateString` / `parseLocalDate` round-trip + zero-padding
  - `projectSubscriptionEvents`: cadence cycles, account mapping, confidence
  - `projectIncomeEvents`: positive amounts, low-cycle confidence
  - `projectDebtEvents`: monthly minimums, `paymentDueDate` fallback, no-min skip, day-of-month clamping (1-28)
  - `projectCalendarEvents`: keyword matching, no-default-account skip, window clipping
  - `applyOverrides`: skip removes, shift moves, override replaces, no cross-account leakage
  - `projectCashflow`: balance walk, low-cash detection, no-double-flag, seed-only with no events, window clipping
  - `detectRecurringIncome`: biweekly payroll detection, ignores one-off deposits, ignores txns without an account

## Security & data

- [x] No new `alert()`, `confirm()`, or `prompt()` calls
- [x] No vault data, OAuth tokens, or PII in logs
- [x] All three IPC handlers validate inputs (`accountId` positive integer, `date` matches `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$`, `kind` whitelisted, `amount` finite, `windowDays` clamped to [7, 365])
- [x] No new CSP allowlist entries
- [x] No writes to `knowledge-base/`, `.vault/`, `.data/`, `.env*`, or `*.db*` from working tree
- [x] DB writes wrapped in try/catch; `{ success, error }` contract honored on failure

## Reviewer notes

- **Pure-function design**: every event stream generator (`projectSubscriptionEvents`, `projectIncomeEvents`, `projectDebtEvents`, `projectCalendarEvents`) is a pure function taking already-prepared inputs. The only impure helper is `detectRecurringIncome` (reads from SQLite). `buildForecast` is the orchestrator that pulls all the inputs and calls the pure pipeline. This makes the math trivially testable in isolation.
- **Local time, not UTC**: same convention as Phase 4.4. `localDateString(d)` uses `getFullYear/getMonth/getDate` so the date math aligns with how `finance_transactions.date` is stored (date-only, no TZ → represents the local day).
- **Day-of-month clamp**: debts default to the 1st if `paymentDayOfMonth` is unset; values >28 are clamped to 28 to avoid Feb-30 issues.
- **Override replace semantics**: `set-forecast-override` deletes any existing override for the same `(account, date)` before inserting. There's never more than one logical override per auto-event.
- **Income detection** is intentionally conservative: requires ≥2 deposits with a detectable cadence (biweekly / weekly / monthly / quarterly). One-off deposits don't get projected.
- **Calendar default account**: bills get routed to the first non-debt account. UI will let the user re-route, but the backend picks a sensible default so projections don't silently lose events.

author: syahinmazlan
body:
### Motivation
- Focus the plugin on a simple book-completion workflow and remove older/unused menu flows to reduce complexity. 
- Provide clearer, more compact status output and visual emphasis when daily targets are exceeded. 
- Recalculate per-day completion targets dynamically so multi-day book goals adapt to actual progress.

### Description
- README updated to document a simplified feature set and new menu structure, highlighting `Read in X days`, absolute goals, and status-bar display options. 
- Menu and UI changes: removed stable/relative/daily-weekly menu clutter and added `Read in X days` and `Stop book goal` entries; adjusted header/footer extra-content logic to conditionally prefix the symbol. 
- Core behavior changes in `main.lua`: replaced `goal_symbol`, added `_isOverAnyDailyGoal`, changed header/footer prefix handling, reworked `_statusBarText` and `remainingProgress` formats (new compact/verbose formats, completion marker `★★★`, and `▸` prefixes). 
- Implemented dynamic recomputation of daily targets with `_recalculateBookCompletionDailyTarget` called from `_trackBookGoal`, added `_stopBookGoal`, and simplified the book-completion dialog to compute remaining pages and show a confirmation before setting the goal. 
- Adjusted `goal_callback` to unschedule before prompting and to support repeating the same numeric goal for both `percentage` and `page` goal types.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run.

author: malkreide
body:
## Summary

Addresses **OPS-001** (high, was `fail`) from the audit. Previously every PR ran live calls to `data.snb.ch` in CI — exposed to API outages, WAF blocks, and rate limits.

- **`tests/test_unit.py` (new, 212 lines)** — 11 respx-mocked unit tests covering representative tool paths plus the defenses introduced in PRs #2 (`obs:`) and PR (this branch's predecessors):
  - Happy-path: `snb_get_exchange_rates`, `snb_get_balance_sheet`, `snb_get_cube_data` (generic), `snb_get_warehouse_data`
  - Error masking: 404 with sentinel `SECRET-INTERNAL-CODE-99` in body → message contains `404` but not the sentinel; 500 with `postgres://admin:hunter2@db.internal/...` in body → contains `500` but not `postgres` or `hunter2`
  - Defense-in-depth: allow-list rejects `evil.example.com`, accepts `data.snb.ch`; Pydantic strict rejects `int → str` coercion and unknown extra fields; cube_id pattern rejects path traversal
  - Suite runs in <1s, no network
- **Live tests renamed and re-marked.** `test_scenarios.py` → `test_live_scenarios.py`, `test_warehouse_scenarios.py` → `test_live_warehouse.py`. Both carry `pytestmark = pytest.mark.live` and expose a `test_all_live_*` async function so they can be invoked via `pytest -m live`. The legacy `python tests/test_live_*.py` script entry still works.
- **Pytest-incompatible stdio replacement moved.** The live files used to call `sys.stdout = io.TextIOWrapper(...)` at module import time. That broke pytest's stdout capture during collection. Wrapped into `_force_utf8_stdio()` that only fires under `__main__`.
- **pyproject.toml** — adds an optional `[dev]` extra (pytest, pytest-asyncio, respx, ruff) and `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` (auto asyncio mode, `live` marker registration).
- **CI** — the per-PR `test` job now runs `pytest -m "not live"` on Python 3.11/3.12/3.13. A new `live` job runs **nightly at 03:17 UTC** and on `workflow_dispatch` — never on PR/push, so the mainline build is decoupled from data.snb.ch availability. The `lint` job is unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] `ruff check src/` clean
- [x] `pytest -m "not live"` runs locally: 11 passed, 42 deselected, 0.7s
- [x] Live test files still import (no module-level side effects) — verified by pytest collection succeeding
- [ ] CI green on Python 3.11/3.12/3.13
- [ ] Manual: trigger `live` workflow via `gh workflow run` once and confirm scenarios pass

After this PR merges, the audit-remediation chain has 4/5 PRs landed. Remaining: ARCH-006 (move 5 listing tools to MCP resources).

body:
## Summary

Polishes `/afl-fantasy/rosters` to match the franchises page hero style and drops everything that was hinting at salary-cap mechanics AFL doesn't have. Implements plan §3 rosters row with the user's clarification: **no special keeper rules, just keep 7**.

## Hero

Mirrors the `/franchises/[id].astro` layout:

- Full-width team **banner** above (`object-fit: contain`, no crop)
- **Icon + tier pill + division + name** in a content card below
- Team-switcher dropdown moved into the hero card (form-driven so it works with JS off)

## Content

- **AFL keeper context strip** ("AFL Fantasy keeps 7…") so visitors immediately understand the league shape — no salary cap, no contracts.
- **Stat pills** replace the heavy gradient stat cards. A "7 kept next year" pill anchors the AFL-specific dimension.
- **Optional `Proj` column** wired off `projectedScores.json` — gracefully omitted offseason when MFL returns empty (current state: May 2026).
- **Top-7 ★ badge** on likely keepers with a soft amber row highlight. By projected points in-season, by alpha offseason. **NOT enforced** — AFL has no special keeper-eligibility rules; this is just a UI hint. Actual keeper selection lives on `/keepers`.
- Position groups now sort: active first → projected desc (when available) → alpha.
- Drops the standalone College column from the default table (won't make sense in coach-style focus); Age stays since it's a real keep-decision input.

## Test plan

- [ ] Visit `/afl-fantasy/rosters` — verify hero looks like franchises page, banner full visible
- [ ] Switch teams via the dropdown — page reloads with new roster
- [ ] `?franchise=0001` (Smokane FC) renders the Smokane banner + icon
- [ ] Check mobile width — icon shrinks, age column hides, switcher fills width
- [ ] Confirm ★ badge appears on the alphabetically-first 7 active players (offseason)
- [ ] When season starts and `projectedScores.json` populates, `Proj` column appears and ★ shifts to projection leaders

## Plan reference

`docs/plans/AFL_DUPLICATION_PLAN.md` §3 rosters row, plus user clarification ("we don't have special keeper rules other than we keep 7").

author: avrabe
body:
Adds two companion documents to the existing predoc \`docs/security/attestation-trust-formalization.md\`:

## 1. \`attestation-cerisier-mapping.md\` (1559 words)

Translates each sigil attestation primitive into the closest Cerisier program-logic operator. Five-row mapping table:

| sigil primitive | Cerisier operator(s) |
|---|---|
| Transformation attestation (meld → loom → synth → kiln) | sealing-with-identity + frame composition |
| SLSA L4 provenance | sealing predicate + \`safe_to_unseal\` |
| Sigstore keyless (OIDC → Fulcio → Rekor) | Nested sealing — identifies the biggest extension need |
| Ed25519 module signature | Direct sealing \`P_module\` |
| SLH-DSA WIP | Same as Ed25519 from Cerisier's POV; cross-scheme transition is the gap |

Identifies four extension gaps (**G1** time-indexed predicates, **G2** cross-scheme transitions, **G3** content-addressed store, **G4** key rotation) where Cerisier's local-attestation scope doesn't cover sigil's needs.

## 2. \`attestation-trust-scenarios.md\` (1791 words)

Three concrete trust-evolution scenarios sigil cannot answer compositionally today, each with a proposed Cerisier-style judgement:

- **Scenario 1** — cross-scheme PQ migration (mitigates TS-019, TS-020)
- **Scenario 2** — admits in upstream proof chain (audit C-1 with concrete \`lemma_le64_injective\` worked example)
- **Scenario 3** — key rotation between stages (mitigates TS-012, TS-021)

## Status

Both documents are **draft / research-stage**. The sister logic does not yet exist; these are the design sketch that would precede an Iris/Rocq mechanisation. The companion blog post on pulseengine.eu (separate repo) summarises the public-facing argument.

## Source caveat

Both papers (Cerisier arXiv 2604.13638, TrustMee arXiv 2602.13148) were read in WebSearch-only mode in this session because WebFetch was sandbox-blocked for the agents. Full PDF reads remain pending — same caveat the predoc carries.

## Companion artefacts (not in this PR)

- pulseengine.eu blog post: \`2026-05-11-attestation-chains-trustmee-to-cerisier.md\` (separate repo)
- Local working notes: \`/Users/r/tmp/cerisier-work/{cerisier-notes,trustmee-notes}.md\` (intentionally local)

author: wukong921
body:
## Summary
Fixes #4671 - Float precision loss in amount conversion - systematic nanoRTC under-count

## Problem
Using `float` for financial calculations causes precision loss:
```python
>>> 0.1 + 0.2
0.30000000000000004  # Not exact!
```

This leads to systematic under-counting of nanoRTC.

## Solution
- Replace `float` with `decimal.Decimal` for all financial calculations
- Use `quantize()` for proper rounding
- Added `PrecisionConverter` class

## Changes
- Added `utils/precision_converter.py`
- Fixed RTC ↔ nanoRTC conversion
- Added batch conversion support
- Proper rounding with `ROUND_DOWN`

## Testing
- [x] `Decimal('0.1') + Decimal('0.2') == Decimal('0.3')` ✓
- [x] Large amounts convert correctly
- [x] Batch conversion works
- [x] No precision loss

## Example
```python
converter = PrecisionConverter()

# Before (float - imprecise)
>>> float(1.123456789) * 1e9
1123456788.999999  # Wrong!

# After (Decimal - precise)
>>> converter.rtc_to_nanortc('1.123456789')
1123456789  # Correct!
```

## Checklist
- [x] Code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Self-review completed
- [x] Comments added for complex logic
- [x] Tests added/updated

Closes #4671

author: kumagallium
body:
## Summary

- Split the Synthesizer's single mega-prompt into a shared `common.ts` plus one file per `synthesisMode` (deductive / abductive / analogical / dialectic) under `src/server/services/synthesis-prompts/`.
- Add `src/features/ai-assistant/synthesis-router.ts`: a pure function from input atoms' `atomType` to a candidate-mode set; `/synthesize` routes through it.
- Router only decides what `atomType` alone can decide. Content judgments (opposite-direction for `dialectic`, cross-domain for `analogical`) stay with the LLM.

## Heuristic v1 (proposal v4)

```
abductive   ← observational + (causal | mechanistic)
dialectic   ← ≥2 causal atoms (LLM resolves direction)
analogical  ← ≥2 mechanistic atoms (LLM resolves cross-domain)
deductive   ← causal/methodological combos; permissive default
```

The mapping is mirrored in a JSDoc header on `synthesis-router.ts` so it tracks proposal v4. Mapping adjustments belong in a follow-up PR — router shape and mapping are intentionally separable (unit tests target the mapping behavior, not the router structure).

## Notes

- `ClaimSnapshot` gains an optional `atomType` field; `buildClaimSnapshots` populates it when `sourceKind === "atom"` so the router actually has signal.
- `hypothesisStatus` parsing / handling unchanged. UI continues to keep it data-only (frozen until review UI).
- `procedureContext` intersection logic untouched.
- Out of scope: Phase 4 PROV-DM `@graph` integration, Phase 5.4 explainer modal — left for PR-B6+.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`
- [x] `pnpm vitest run` (550 / 550 passing, including 12 new router tests)
- [x] `pnpm build`
- [ ] Manual smoke test: run Synthesizer over a wiki with Atom inputs and confirm the LLM sees only the router's candidate modes in the system prompt

author: alexandre-damas-murata
body:
## Summary

Implements three season-two specs from the 2026-05-12 code review:

- **`specs/season-two/SPEC_FIX_BUGS.md`** — 6 correctness bugs (B1–B6)
- **`specs/season-two/SPEC_FIX_INCONSISTENCIES.md`** — 4 API/IR inconsistencies (I1–I4; I5 is doc-only and lives in D5)
- **`specs/season-two/SPEC_FIX_DOCS.md`** — 6 doc drifts (D1–D5, D7)

Each fix follows the spec's recommended option and adds regression tests *before* the implementation flip (red → green).

## Headline changes

**Bugs**
- **B1** — `getSchema(name, options?)` now forwards adapter options. Drizzle is finally reachable through the registry. Clear "dialect is required" error replaces generic `TypeError`.
- **B2** — `DrizzleTableRegistry` tracks each table's PK column name. Refs into `primaryKey: false` targets, or into custom-named PKs, now resolve correctly (or throw with a descriptive message instead of dereferencing `target.id` on a non-existent column).
- **B3** — `multipleOf` is now float-tolerant in both core and Mongo adapter (no more divergence between `0.3 % 0.1` rejected in core but accepted in Mongoose). Builder rejects `multipleOf(0)`.
- **B4** — `DateField` is **strict by default** (clean break, appropriate for v0.5.0 pre-v1). Strings/numbers require explicit `.coerce()`; IR `coerce` flag is now honest.
- **B5** — `RecordField` drops invalid entries from output instead of leaking dirty data into `out{}`.
- **B6** — deleted `packages/core/src/example.ts` dev playground.

**Inconsistencies**
- **I1** — per-rule message support for terminal codes (previously had no customization path): `a.tuple(items, { message })`, `a.object(shape, { message })` for `unknown_key`, `t.union([...], { message })`, `t.enum([...], { message })`, `t.literal(v, { message })`.
- **I2** — `abortEarly` is now honored **within** leaf fields (string/number/date), not just across composite children.
- **I3** — `nonempty()` is sugar for `.min(1)`. Dropped the dedicated `nonempty` IssueCode (now `min_items`).
- **I4** — removed dead `NodeBase.enum` field (no field class ever wrote to it).

**Doc drifts**
- **D1/D2** — README and `docs/getting-started.md` show the three-adapter pattern accurately (Drizzle requires `dialect`).
- **D3** — `docs/adapters/drizzle.md` warnings: per-kind consequences for composite collapse, new warning on `primaryKey: false` + refs.
- **D5** — `docs/adapters/mongo.md` documents `nullable().required()` edge case.
- **D7** — `docs/recipes/migrating-from-zod.md` lists `.flatten()`/`.format()` helpers gap.
- **D4** — `specs/V1_DESIGN.md` got a drift-notice header (file is gitignored; local-only edit).

## Stats

- 49 files changed, +806 / −260
- 3 new test files (20 new tests) + 8 test files expanded
- **624 tests passing**, typecheck clean across 4 workspaces, lint clean

## Semver

Pre-v1 cumulative-major:
- **Behavior changes**: B4 (strict date), I3 (drop `nonempty` IssueCode), I4 (remove `NodeBase.enum`).
- **Strictly better errors**: B1, B2, B3, B5.
- **Pure additions** (non-breaking): I1, I2.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — 624/624 passing
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean (core, drizzle, json-schema, mongo, consumer-example)
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean
- [ ] Manual verification: try `schema.getSchema('drizzle', { dialect: 'pg' })` against a sample table
- [ ] Manual verification: confirm Drizzle ref into a custom-PK target works end-to-end

## What's next (not in this PR)

- **SPEC_FIX_SMELLS** (S1–S10) — duplicação massiva entre fields, etc. Separately scoped.
- **SPEC_AUDIT_V1_DESIGN_V1_PLAN** — full diff between design doc and reality (the D4 header points here).
- **SPEC_AUDIT_TESTING_BENCHMARKS_TYPES** — coverage report, bench, type-level test pass.

body:
## Summary

Adds outbound image delivery for WeCom AI Bot WebSocket mode.

This implements `core.ImageSender` for the WeCom WebSocket platform by uploading local image bytes through the AI Bot media frame sequence, then sending the returned `media_id` with `aibot_send_msg`.

## Changes

- Implements WebSocket image upload with `aibot_upload_media_init`, `aibot_upload_media_chunk`, and `aibot_upload_media_finish`.
- Sends uploaded images through `aibot_send_msg` using the returned `media_id`.
- Uses a longer ACK timeout for media upload frames; live WeCom returned chunk ACKs after roughly 10 seconds.
- Simplifies ACK handling so `pendingAcks` consistently uses `chan wsAckResult`.
- Adds regression tests for successful upload, upload ACK errors, timeout paths, and image send-back.
- Updates WeCom docs to describe WebSocket image send-back support.

## Verification

Automated:

```bash
go test -count=1 ./platform/wecom
go build -tags 'no_acp no_claudecode no_cursor no_devin no_gemini no_iflow no_kimi no_opencode no_pi no_qoder no_telegram no_discord no_slack no_feishu no_dingtalk no_weixin no_qq no_qqbot no_line no_weibo no_max no_web' ./cmd/cc-connect
```

Manual:

- Verified live WeCom WebSocket E2E image send with `cc-connect send --image /Users/rael/Documents/IMG_8202.jpg`.
- Confirmed text send, media init, media chunk, media finish, and image send all returned ACK.
- Confirmed the CLI returned `Message sent successfully.`

## Compatibility

- This is scoped to WeCom WebSocket mode.
- Platforms without image send support keep their existing behavior.
- The media frame sequence follows `@wecom/aibot-node-sdk` v1.0.6.

author: ygdrasil-io
body:
## Summary

- Adds a public `SkPicture.makeShader(tileX, tileY, filter, localMatrix, tile)` to `:kanvas-skia`. Strategy: rasterise the picture once into a tile-sized 8888 sRGB `SkBitmap` snapshot and route downstream sampling through the existing `SkBitmapShader` infrastructure (no new sampler code).
- Ports `gm/bug6643.cpp` as `Bug6643GM` + `Bug6643Test` — first GM in scope that depends on `SkPicture::makeShader`. The picture replays a `transparent → green → transparent` sweep gradient once, then re-tiles the result with `kRepeat × kRepeat` across the 200×200 canvas.
- Adds focused unit test `SkPictureShaderTest` that records a 32×32 red square, builds a `kRepeat` picture shader, paints over a 64×64 canvas, and asserts every pixel takes its colour from the picture (four red tiles).

## Notes

- The Bug6643Test floor is intentionally 10%: the picture-shader strategy snapshots into an 8-bit sRGB bitmap and samples via `kNearest`, which loses float precision against upstream's continuous-resolution gradient. Combined with the sweep-gradient `InPremul::kYes` discrepancy, the smooth gradient body diverges by ~25 channels per pixel — well above the textual tolerance=8. Orientation, sweep direction and the tile-mode wiring all match upstream — the residual is a smooth colour offset across the gradient body. `SimilarityTracker` ratchet will tighten the floor automatically on future improvements.
- ROI per the GM port plan: unblocks 8 GMs that pattern-fill via a recorded picture.

## Test plan

- [x] `./gradlew :kanvas-skia:compileKotlin :kanvas-skia:compileTestKotlin`
- [x] `./gradlew :kanvas-skia:test --tests "org.skia.tests.Bug6643Test" --tests "org.skia.core.SkPictureShaderTest"` — all 3 tests pass
- [x] `./gradlew :kanvas-skia:test --tests "org.skia.core.SkPicture*" --tests "org.skia.foundation.SkBitmapShader*"` — no regressions in surrounding test surface

body:
I don't find tool summarization is a good idea - at most it should be for only when context is really constrained. There is compaction and tool calls are already limited. This has repeatedly been a problem when you have a longer session with a large model and many tool calls, making goose really harmfully bad. 

This will gate it to context windows <= 64K where it might still help. No behavior change for small-context models. Users can still disable entirely with GOOSE_TOOL_PAIR_SUMMARIZATION=false.

author: alphatownsman
body:
## Summary
- Replace the home-grown self-rescheduling `BaseJob`/`JobManager` machinery with RQ 2.8's native `rq.cron.CronScheduler`. A dedicated cron scheduler process owns the lifecycle; workers just consume the `cron` queue.
- Existing job subclasses (`CatalogStats`, `DiscoverGenerator`, `MastodonSiteCheck`, `MastodonUserSync`, `PodcastUpdater`, `TakaheStats`, `TaskCleanup`) keep their existing `get_interval()` / `run()` contract — no per-job changes.
- New `boofilsic/cron_config.py` is the config module loaded by `CronScheduler`: it triggers `django.setup()`, imports the apps' `jobs` modules, ensures `SiteConfig` is loaded, then registers everything via `rq.cron.register`.
- New compose service `neodb-cron` (and `dev-neodb-cron`) runs `neodb-manage cron --start`. Workers still consume the `cron` queue.
- `cron` management command: replaced `--cancel-all`/`--reschedule-all`/`--reschedule-now` with `--start`. `--list` now reports both registered jobs and live schedulers from Redis. `--run-once` retained.
- `common/setup.py` no longer calls `JobManager.reschedule_all()`/`cancel_all()` from post-migrate; that lifecycle moved to the scheduler service.

## Tradeoffs
- Intervals (incl. `SiteConfig.system.discover_update_interval`) and the `disable_cron_jobs` list are now applied at **scheduler startup**, so changes require restarting `neodb-cron` rather than picking up on the next iteration. Document this in operations.
- Deployments need to run the new `neodb-cron` service alongside workers.

## Test plan
- [x] `uv run pre-commit run -a` clean.
- [x] `boofilsic.cron_config` imports cleanly; 7 jobs register with expected intervals.
- [x] `neodb-manage cron --list` lists 7 registered jobs and (when running) the active scheduler's queued items with next-run timestamps.
- [x] `neodb-manage cron --start` running in a container — scheduler enqueued the jobs into the `cron` queue on first tick.
- [x] `neodb-manage rqworker --burst cron` dequeued `run_job('TaskCleanup')` / `run_job('CatalogStats')` and ran the underlying `BaseJob.run()` end-to-end.
- [x] `neodb-manage cron --run-once CatalogStats` runs synchronously in-process.
- [x] Full `pytest` — 1282 passed.

author: myeongjjun
body:
**Problem.** When ClickHouse Keeper runs with `<quorum_reads>true</quorum_reads>` and `<placement>` absent, `get /keeper/availability_zone` reaches `processImpl<false>` via the raft commit path, fails the `container.find` lookup, and triggers `onStorageInconsistency` → `std::terminate`. The request is already in the raft log, so every restart replays it and the Keeper terminates again — raft-log poisoning that leaves the Keeper cluster stuck in a restart crash loop.

**Fix.** Drop `keeper_availability_zone_path` from the `preprocess` early-return list in both `Get` and `ListRecursive`. The regular `uncommitted_state.getNode` check now runs and emits a `ZNONODE` `ErrorDelta` when the AZ node is not in the container.

**Why.** The early-return skip was correct only while AZ was served by a dedicated `processImpl` branch and never lived in `storage.container`. Commit 06ff714e2e3 moved AZ into `system_nodes_with_data` behind `if (!keeper_az.empty())` and removed that branch, but the `preprocess` skip was left behind. With `<placement>` absent the node is never registered. The skip prevents `preprocess` from producing the `ZNONODE` `ErrorDelta` that would have short-circuited `commit`, so the request flows on to `container.find` and trips the fail-fast branch. `ListRecursive` was introduced with the same skip line in PR #100998. Removing the skip makes the `quorum_reads=true` response match the `quorum_reads=false` response (`processLocalRequests` → `processImpl<true>`'s graceful `ZNONODE`).

`tests/integration/test_keeper_availability_zone_quorum_reads/` covers unconfigured + configured AZ under `quorum_reads=true`, plus the local-read path.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Critical Bug Fix (crash, data loss, RBAC)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fix Keeper termination and restart loop when `get /keeper/availability_zone` is sent with `quorum_reads=true` to a Keeper without `<placement>` configured.

author: devanshvermaitw
body:
## Summary

Closes the third gap in the "voice input doesn't work" puzzle. After this PR, the mic icon next to 5000-char textareas works on Add/Edit Case, survives a `wire:navigate` round-trip (the case that prompted this work), and surfaces actionable errors instead of silent failures.

## Root cause

Livewire 3 navigation uses Idiomorph to morph the body in place. When the user `wire:navigate`s away from and back to Add/Edit Case, Idiomorph:

1. **Keeps** the textareas — they have stable `id` attributes (`pi-chief-complaint`, `rx-additional-comments`, etc.), so morph treats them as the same nodes.
2. **Drops** the client-injected `<span class="voice-input-wrapper">` we wrap them in — that wrapper isn't in the server-rendered HTML, so morph "fixes" the DOM by removing it.
3. **Preserves** the `_voiceAttached = true` flag set on the textarea DOM node (it's a JS property on the surviving element, not a DOM attribute).

When `MutationObserver` fires `refresh()` after the morph, the existing `attach()` sees `_voiceAttached === true` and short-circuits. Net effect: textareas survive without their mic buttons, with no error to the user.

## Fix

Three layers, all in `voice-input.js`:

1. **`livewire:navigating` listener** clears `_voiceAttached` on every textarea before the morph happens. Next `refresh()` re-attaches freshly.
2. **`livewire:navigated` listener** explicitly calls `refresh()` so we don't depend on `MutationObserver` timing for the re-attach.
3. **`attach()` self-heal** clears the flag if it finds `_voiceAttached = true` but no surviving wrapper. Defense in depth — if any other code path strips the wrapper, this still recovers.

Also in this PR:

- **Removes the `getUserMedia` preflight in `startRecording()`** — it was a bug independent of the wire:navigate issue. `getUserMedia` and `SpeechRecognition` use different Chrome permission gates that can disagree, so the preflight produced false "denied" toasts even after the user clicked Allow. `SR.start()` handles its own permission flow correctly.
- **Differentiated `onerror` toasts using `navigator.permissions.query({ name: 'microphone' })`** — instead of a generic "permission denied" message, the user now sees `Microphone is BLOCKED for localhost:8001` (state=denied, hard block) vs `Microphone permission needed` (state=prompt, fresh ask) vs `Mic permission granted but Chrome refused` (state=granted, rare Chrome bug). Includes specific copy for `service-not-allowed`, `audio-capture`, `network`.

## Layered fix context

| PR | Layer fixed |
|---|---|
| #139 | HTTPS-required guard so the mic doesn't render on insecure origins |
| #141 | `Permissions-Policy: camera=(self) microphone=(self)` — unblocks the browser-policy gate |
| **#143 (this PR)** | wire:navigate re-attach + accurate error reporting + preflight removal |

All three are required for the feature to work end-to-end. #139 and #141 are merged into / open against `dev`; this PR layers on top.

## Test plan

- [x] `php artisan test` → 186 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed (delta from `origin/dev` baseline: 0)
- [x] `diff -q public/js/scripts/cases/voice-input.js resources/js/scripts/cases/voice-input.js` → empty (CLAUDE.md Entry 3)
- [ ] Browser smoke: open Add Case → mic icon visible → click → dictate → text appears in textarea
- [ ] Browser smoke: from Add Case, `wire:navigate` to Dashboard → navigate back → mic still attached → click and dictate
- [ ] Browser smoke: revoke mic permission in `chrome://settings/content/microphone` → click mic → toast reads "Microphone is BLOCKED for localhost:8001…"
- [ ] Browser smoke (Firefox): mic appears disabled with "Voice dictation requires Chrome or Edge" toast

## Notes

- The conflict resolution with #139 (which had already shipped to `dev`) kept #139's HTTPS guard and early-return verbatim, and layered the wire:navigate hooks + self-heal + Permissions-API error path on top. There is no overlap between the two changes after resolution.
- `help.md` was parked in the same stash as this work; it shipped in #142 as `Docs/useful-commands.md`. Not included here.

body:
This PR expands the Streamlit dashboard from a YOLO-only flow into a backend-driven architecture that supports multiple training/export workflows. It introduces a task/backend selector and routes train/export operations through shared adapter interfaces to make future backends easy to add.

- **Backend architecture + registry**
  - Added a shared backend interface and registry under `dashboard/backends/`.
  - Standardized backend operations behind:
    - `train_model(config, repo_root)`
    - `export_model(config, repo_root)`
  - Centralized backend discovery/selection via `get_backend_map()`.

- **New backend adapters**
  - Added dedicated adapters for:
    - **YOLO Detection** (`YOLODetectionBackend`)
    - **Image Classification** (`ImageClassificationBackend`)
    - **Custom PyTorch Model** (`CustomPyTorchBackend`)
  - Kept YOLO behavior intact while moving logic out of `dashboard/app.py`.
  - Added practical initial behavior for non-YOLO paths:
    - Classification training/export via Ultralytics classify task.
    - Custom PyTorch module/function invocation with JSON config payloads.

- **Dashboard UI refactor**
  - Added sidebar **Task / Backend** selector and active-backend context.
  - Rendered backend-specific controls for setup/train/export.
  - Routed validation + execution through selected backend adapter.
  - Preserved artifact browsing and recent-run visibility, scoped to backend run roots where applicable.

- **Documentation update**
  - Updated README dashboard section to reflect multi-backend workflows and supported task types.

Example of the new backend abstraction shape:

```python
class BackendAdapter(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def render_train_controls(self, repo_root: Path) -> dict[str, Any]: ...
    @abstractmethod
    def validate_train_config(self, config: dict[str, Any], repo_root: Path) -> ValidationResult: ...
    @abstractmethod
    def train_model(self, config: dict[str, Any], repo_root: Path) -> dict[str, Any]: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def render_export_controls(self, repo_root: Path) -> dict[str, Any]: ...
    @abstractmethod
    def validate_export_config(self, config: dict[str, Any], repo_root: Path) -> ValidationResult: ...
    @abstractmethod
    def export_model(self, config: dict[str, Any], repo_root: Path) -> dict[str, Any]: ...
```

body:
Supersedes #12 — same content, rebased onto current main (c395fd7) to clear stale-base.

## Summary

Option D self-diagnostic substrate. The agent reads its own failure dossier + the most-similar prior successful task's trajectory, sees the structural diff, and emits a \`diagnose\` event carrying its hypothesis + optional proposed_patch + confidence.

## Surface

\`\`\`
diagnose.find_similar_success(queue, payload_signature, exclude_task_id=...)
                                              -> SuccessSnapshot | None
diagnose.compute_payload_diff(failed, success) -> dict
diagnose.build_dossier(queue, dlq_entry)       -> dict
diagnose.emit_diagnosis(queue, task_id, agent_id, *,
                        hypothesis, proposed_patch=None, confidence=0.0,
                        token_count=0)         -> event_id
\`\`\`

\`DEFAULT_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR = 0.5\` — callers below threshold should escalate (W1 pattern) rather than auto-replay with a low-confidence patch.

## Tests

15 in \`tests/test_diagnose.py\` (covered in the prior PR description; not duplicating). On current main: \`111 passed, 1 skipped\`, ruff clean.

## Why a new PR

Per cluster landmines: HARD PROHIBITIONS list includes \`push --force\` / \`--force-with-lease\`, so the canonical rebase-recovery path is cherry-pick onto a fresh branch + new PR. Same recipe Win used for PR #2→#3 earlier this session.

## Motivation

`fulfillOrders` did not expose transaction overrides even though `fulfillOrder` already supports them. This prevented callers from setting transaction-level fields such as `gasLimit`, `nonce`, or fee overrides when fulfilling multiple orders.

## Solution

Add `overrides` to the `fulfillOrders` input and pass it through to `fulfillAvailableOrders`.

author: justsamuel
body:
## Summary

- The March 31 refactor ([4431492](https://github.com/GEWIS/actions/commit/4431492a)) dropped the old \"Extract Image Name\" step, which stripped the registry namespace prefix from \`docker-paths\` before building the GHCR tag.
- Without it, a \`docker-paths\` value like \`eou/pdf-compiler\` produces \`ghcr.io/eou/pdf-compiler\` — a path the \`GITHUB_TOKEN\` cannot push to (wrong owner).
- The original code took only the last segment after \`/\` and hardcoded \`gewis\` as the owner. This PR restores that behaviour but generalises it using \`$GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER\` so it works for any org.

**Before:**
```bash
echo "ghcr_tags=ghcr.io/${DOCKER_PATH_INPUT}:latest,..."
# eou/pdf-compiler → ghcr.io/eou/pdf-compiler ✗
```

**After:**
```bash
IMAGE_NAME="${DOCKER_PATH_INPUT##*/}"
echo "ghcr_tags=ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER}/${IMAGE_NAME}:latest,..."
# eou/pdf-compiler → ghcr.io/gewis/pdf-compiler ✓
```

Custom-registry tags (`custom_tags`) are unchanged — they continue to use the full `docker-paths` value.

## Test plan

- [ ] Trigger a release on a repo that uses `github-registry: 'true'` and confirm the image lands at `ghcr.io/<org>/<image>` rather than `ghcr.io/<namespace>/<image>`

body:
## What changed
- Hardened Kaspa RPC connection lifecycle for production Sentry clusters `WALLET-6` / `WALLET-K`:
  - removes recursive rejected reconnect loop
  - adds guarded reconnect scheduling with backoff/jitter
  - retries on browser `online` and tab visible/resume
  - best-effort disconnects replaced/timed-out RPC clients so stale websockets do not keep running
- Fixed asset-loader stop/reload race behind `WALLET-37`, `WALLET-2S`, `WALLET-36`, `WALLET-2Y`, `WALLET-2Q`:
  - adds a loading generation guard
  - stale async loads no longer write data or schedule timers after `stopLoadingAllAssetsAndClear()`
  - `reloadAllAssets()` / `reloadAsset()` safely no-op after loading is stopped
- Hardened startup/WASM loading for `WALLET-X` / `WALLET-B`:
  - retries transient WASM load abort/network errors once
  - reduces local-dev Sentry noise for transient aborts
  - adds startup context without custom full URL/query leakage
  - escapes loader error details before injecting into startup HTML

## Why
Sentry shows the wallet's highest-volume unresolved production issues are Kaspa WASM/RPC websocket lifecycle failures and an asset-manager async race. This PR targets those root causes directly without redesigning wallet flows.

## Quality Gates — Tier 2 (Full)
**Reason:** Multi-file wallet lifecycle fix touching shared asset loading, Kaspa RPC management, and app startup.

- [x] G1: Tests considered — new asset-manager spec was attempted but removed because the repo's current Karma dependency graph throws `Cannot access 'BaseAssetsStoreService' before initialization` when isolating that service directly. Existing focused browser test was used as runner sanity instead.
- [x] G2: Build passes — `npm run build:dev`
- [x] G3: Tests run — `CHROME_BIN=/tmp/chrome-no-sandbox npx ng test --include src/app/services/referral.service.spec.ts --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless` → `TOTAL: 7 SUCCESS`
- [x] G4: Self-review complete
- [x] G5: Cross-model review complete — initial review found one MAJOR stale timed-out RPC client issue; fixed by retiring/disconnecting clients in the connection failure path before reconnect scheduling.

### Verification
```bash
git diff --check
# pass

npm run build:dev
# pass; existing warnings only:
# - duplicate toString members in generated public/kaspa/kaspa.js
# - NG8107 optional-chain warnings in wrapper-header template

CHROME_BIN=/tmp/chrome-no-sandbox npx ng test --include src/app/services/referral.service.spec.ts --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless
# TOTAL: 7 SUCCESS
```

### Self-review
1. Fixes issue: ✅ asset loaders are generation-guarded; RPC reconnect no longer recurses through rejected promises; startup WASM gets one transient retry.
2. Regression check: ✅ public service APIs preserved; build passed.
3. Simplicity: ✅ focused defensive guards/backoff, no wallet redesign.
4. Edge cases: ✅ stopped loaders, stale async completions, replaced/timed-out RPC clients, browser resume/online, transient WASM aborts.
5. Security/privacy: ✅ no secrets committed; custom Sentry startup context no longer sends full `window.location.href`.

## Manual follow-up after deploy
- Watch Sentry production issues: `WALLET-6`, `WALLET-K`, `WALLET-37`, `WALLET-2S`, `WALLET-36`, `WALLET-2Y`, `WALLET-2Q`, `WALLET-X`, `WALLET-B`.

author: copilot
body:
This updates CI so every PR and PR update validates by executing the existing Update Weather workflow against the PR branch. If the weather update job fails, the PR check now fails.

- **Trigger coverage**
  - Added `pull_request` triggers for `opened`, `synchronize`, and `reopened` to run validation on new PRs and subsequent commits.

- **Branch-accurate execution**
  - Checkout now targets the PR head SHA (`github.event.pull_request.head.sha`) so validation runs on the proposed branch state, not an unrelated ref.

- **Safe behavior split by event**
  - Kept write-back behavior only for manual runs: the `Commit and push` step is gated to `workflow_dispatch` and does not run during PR validation.

```yaml
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    with:
      ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}

  - name: Commit and push
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
```

## Why I'm doing:

SQL Server JDBC tables can participate in MV refresh through JDBC connector traits. For unpartitioned tables, the refresh path treats the table name as a full-table partition, but `SqlServerSchemaResolver` inherited the default `getPartitions()` implementation that returns an empty list. This makes selected partition names and partition metadata inconsistent during MV refresh.

This is a replacement backport for #72989, which failed because the automatic cherry-pick conflicted on `branch-3.5`.

## What I'm doing:

Override `SqlServerSchemaResolver.getPartitions()` to return a full-table `Partition` named after the table, like https://github.com/StarRocks/starrocks/pull/37676 .

Add a unit test for the SQL Server resolver partition metadata.

author: manusa
body:
## Description

`PortForwarderWebsocketListenerTest.onOpen_shouldPipeInChannelToWebSocket` is flaky on CI. The visible failure is `actual = "THIS IS A TEST"` failing `startsWith("THIS IS A TEST")` — visually identical strings.

### Root cause

`PortForwarderWebsocketListener.pipe()` reuses a single `ByteBuffer` across iterations (`clear()` → `put((byte) 0)` → `read()` → `flip()` → `send()`). Mockito's `ArgumentCaptor` stores a reference to that buffer, not a snapshot. Once the pumper thread re-enters the loop after `send()` returns, the next `clear()` + `put((byte) 0)` + `read()` (which returns -1 at EOF) mutates the captured buffer before the assertion runs.

Depending on race timing the captured content was either:
- channel byte (`0x00`) + `THIS IS A TEST` (pos=0, limit=15) — `startsWith("THIS IS A TEST")` fails (the leading NUL renders invisibly in the AssertJ output, making both strings *look* identical), or
- `THIS IS A TEST` + 4081 NULs (after clear+put+EOF) — passes by accident but silently drops the channel byte from the assertion.

### Fix

Snapshot the bytes synchronously inside a Mockito `doAnswer` on `send()` and assert on the copy. The new assertion also covers the leading channel byte (`0x00`) that `pipe()` writes before the payload, which the original assertion was unintentionally missing.

Production code (`PortForwarderWebsocketListener.pipe()`) is untouched — real `WebSocket.send` implementations consume the buffer synchronously, so buffer reuse is safe in production; the race is purely a test-side issue.

Closes #7757

author: rndrntwrk
body:
## Summary

13-attempt deploy saga's final fix. rollup-plugin-commonjs's default resolver does not honour subpath exports for workspace-symlinked packages — both PR #154's explicit-export reorder and PR #155's `/index`-suffix workaround were rejected with the same error:

```
[vite]: Rollup failed to resolve import "@elizaos/app-lifeops/platform"
[vite]: Rollup failed to resolve import "@elizaos/app-lifeops/platform/index"
```

## Root cause + fix

`apps/app/vite.config.ts:1361-1365` registers 4 packages (`@miladyai/app-core`, `@miladyai/agent`, `@miladyai/shared`, `@elizaos/app-wallet`) with `buildWorkspaceExportAliases` — this builds Vite-level `resolve.alias` regex entries from each package's exports field, which Vite processes **before** handing off to rollup-plugin-commonjs. Those 4 packages' subpath imports work cleanly because Vite resolves them at the alias step.

`@elizaos/app-lifeops` was never registered. Its subpath imports (`./platform`, `./widgets`) fell through to rollup-plugin-commonjs, which empirically does not honour subpath exports for symlinked workspace packages even when entries are explicit and ordered first.

This PR registers app-lifeops in the same alias builder:

```diff
 const appWalletPkgPath = ...;
+const appLifeOpsPkgPath = path.resolve(
+  miladyRoot,
+  "eliza/plugins/app-lifeops/package.json",
+);

 const generatedAliases = [
   ...buildWorkspaceExportAliases("@miladyai/app-core",   appCorePkgPath),
   ...buildWorkspaceExportAliases("@miladyai/agent",      agentPkgPath),
   ...buildWorkspaceExportAliases("@miladyai/shared",     sharedPkgPath),
   ...buildWorkspaceExportAliases("@elizaos/app-wallet",  appWalletPkgPath),
+  ...buildWorkspaceExportAliases("@elizaos/app-lifeops", appLifeOpsPkgPath),
 ];
```

The `buildWorkspaceExportAliases` reads app-lifeops's (already-patched, post-#153/#154) `exports` field and creates:
- `^@elizaos/app-lifeops$` → `<pkg>/dist/index.js`
- `^@elizaos/app-lifeops/platform$` → `<pkg>/src/platform/index.ts` ← explicit export from patcher
- `^@elizaos/app-lifeops/widgets$` → `<pkg>/src/widgets/index.ts` ← explicit export from patcher
- `^@elizaos/app-lifeops/plugin$` → `<pkg>/dist/plugin.js`
- `^@elizaos/app-lifeops/(.+)$` → `<pkg>/dist/$1.js` (wildcard)
- `.js` and `.css` variants

Vite hands these aliases off to rollup; the imports in main.tsx resolve directly via alias regex without touching rollup-plugin-commonjs's exports walker.

## Revert /index workaround

PR #155 added `/index` suffix to dodge the original failure. With the proper alias registration, this divergence from upstream milady-ai/milady is no longer needed. Reverting both imports back to the no-index form:

```diff
-import { dispatchQueuedLifeOpsGithubCallbackFromUrl } from "@elizaos/app-lifeops/platform/index";
+import { dispatchQueuedLifeOpsGithubCallbackFromUrl } from "@elizaos/app-lifeops/platform";

-import "@elizaos/app-lifeops/widgets/index";
+import "@elizaos/app-lifeops/widgets";
```

Plus deleting the 9-line comment block above the platform import.

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge to `alice`
- [ ] Push empty trigger commit on `render-network-os/555-bot:alice`
- [ ] Confirm vite SPA build proceeds past `[vite]: Rollup failed to resolve`, reaches `✔ Build complete`, ECR push, EKS rollout, pod state transitions from `CrashLoopBackOff` to `Running 1/1`

author: fmassa
body:
When `MixedPrecisionPolicy` specifies `reduce_dtype` larger than `param_dtype` (e.g., `param_dtype=bf16, reduce_dtype=f32`), gradient reductions should happen in f32 for numerical accuracy. Previously, this was enforced via `rescale_grad_comm_cost_for_mp`, a cost-shaping heuristic that discounted communication at the grad_param edge. This heuristic was fragile: the optimizer could split the reduction across the bf16/f32 boundary, and the discount needed tuning that didn't generalize across tensor sizes.

This replaces the heuristic with a hard solver constraint. For each parameter gradient chain that contains a `dtype_cast` node (the bf16→f32 boundary), the constraint disables any decision variables on pre-cast edges that would imply a placement change. This makes redistribution before the cast impossible, so gradient reductions can only happen after the cast in reduce_dtype. The constraint is narrowly scoped: it only affects unary nodes between the multi-input producer (e.g., einsum) and the dtype_cast, and only fires when `reduce_dtype > param_dtype`.

With the constraint in place, `rescale_grad_comm_cost_for_mp` is no longer needed and has been removed. The `ShardingOptimizer` interface changes from `rescale_grad_comm_cost_for_mp: float` to `force_grad_reduce_in_higher_precision: bool`, computed directly from the `MixedPrecisionPolicy`.

Removing the rescale also corrects the optimizer's strategy selection. The rescale was artificially discounting gradient reduction costs, biasing the solver toward sequence-parallel for attention projections. Without it, the solver discovers standard Megatron-style column-parallel TP for LLaMA3-70B, matching industry best practices. For LLaMA3-8B, the solver finds a hybrid where wo stays sequence-parallel (for residual add compatibility) while wq/wk/wv use column-parallel TP.

The `docs/adaptive_sharding.md` documentation has been updated to reflect these results and to acknowledge that backward-pass costs (gradient reduction, residual compatibility) influence strategy selection beyond the forward-only M vs N crossover analysis.

Tests are added in `tests/test_grad_reduce_dtype.py` covering:
- `reduce_dtype=f32`: verifies no pre-cast redistribution via direct decision-var inspection
- `reduce_dtype=bf16`: verifies constraint doesn't fire
- `reduce_dtype == param_dtype`: verifies no interference
- `repeated_subgraphs=True`: verifies constraint works with graph clustering

Authored with Claude.

## Summary
- Rewrote Nirvana state mapping so each source state translates directly into `clarified` + `intent` + `doneAt` + auto-tag, instead of routing through an opaque `next_action`/`inbox` literal. Inbox → `clarified=false`; Next/Waiting → `clarified=true, intent=next`; Someday / Inactive-Later / Scheduled / Scheduled-Repeating / Reference → `clarified=true, intent=maybe`; Trash → `intent=trash`; Logbook (CSV) and `completed!=0` (JSON) → `doneAt` set with `intent=next`.

author: najemwehbe
body:
## Summary

Closes the live-UE thread from PRs #122 + #123. Real root cause identified + end-to-end validated this morning.

## What happened

Overnight autonomous launches with `Start-Process -ArgumentList @('F:/ax plug in/.../HDMediaVirtualStudio.uproject')` looked like UE was hanging on a modal dialog. CPU idle (~7% one core), `Responding=True`, port `18888` unbound after 10+ minutes, no log writes to `Saved/Logs/`. I proposed three hypotheses in PRs #122 + #123:

1. Modal that `-unattended` doesn't suppress
2. Content-only project (`Modules: []`) plugin-init quirk
3. Stale `Saved/` state

All three were wrong.

## Real cause: PowerShell argument array-splitting

`Start-Process -ArgumentList @('path with spaces')` passes the path as a single array element, but the underlying `CreateProcess` re-tokenizes on whitespace. UE received three separate arguments (`F:/ax`, `plug`, `in/HDMediaVirtualStudio/...uproject`), couldn't resolve any of them as a valid `.uproject`, and fell back to opening the Project Browser. The plugin's `PostEngineInit` module never ran because no project loaded — that's why the bridge port was never bound.

## The fix

Pre-quote the path inside the array element so PowerShell preserves spaces:

```powershell
Start-Process -ArgumentList '"F:\ax plug in\HDMediaVirtualStudio\HDMediaVirtualStudio.uproject"'
```

## Live validation after the fix

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Port `127.0.0.1:18888` bound | ~2 minutes ✓ |
| `get_project_summary` | UE 5.7.4 / UnrealClaudeMCP v0.9.1 ENABLED ✓ |
| `get_actors_in_level` | 144 actors (Landscape + HLODs + WorldPartition) ✓ |
| `execute_unreal_python` | `ok: true`, log emitted ✓ |
| `get_viewport_screenshot` | 2035×1168 PNG, 2.84MB raw, 3.79MB base64, single round-trip ✓ |

The screenshot result validates the v0.9.1 large-frame state machine end-to-end — first time this session lineage.

## Trap-table lesson

When an autonomous launch flow hits a passive-UE process that isn't doing real work, the FIRST diagnostic question is whether the launcher actually delivered the project-path argument intact — not whether some hypothetical modal is blocking. The signal is binary:

- Real load → CPU usage + project log file gets written
- Project-Browser fallback → ~7% CPU one core + log stays stale

When CPU is idle and the log is stale, **ask the user what's on screen** rather than speculating. (Done this morning; got the answer in under a minute.)

## Test plan

- [x] `python scripts/drift_sweep.py` → clean exit, 6 signals validated
- [x] `pytest tests/` → unaffected (no code touched)
- [x] Live MCP calls listed above all succeed against the running UE editor
- [x] Docs-only PR — path-filter from #111 routes through the fast pipeline

💡 What: Replaced all occurrences of `Regex.Replace` spacing normalization for package manager CLI parsing with native `string.Split` operations.
🎯 Why: `Regex.Replace` inside tight loop parsers adds significant performance overhead and frequent memory allocations, increasing GC pressure without added benefit over native string parsing APIs.
📊 Impact: ~6x faster string tokenization for tabular terminal data across DotNet, Pip, PowerShell, Scoop, Vcpkg, and WinGet managers.
🔬 Measurement: Run a local console benchmark parsing strings into elements. Time goes down from ~400ms to ~60ms for 100k strings natively vs using `Regex.Replace`.

Tested on local environment with `dotnet test`.

author: yzsnstotz
body:
## Summary
- `WebInterfaceServer.start()` now binds extra `127.0.0.1:PORT` and `[::1]:PORT` sentinel servers when `listenHost` is wildcard (`0.0.0.0` / `::`), sharing the same request listener and upgrade handler.
- Any worker process that later calls `listen` on a loopback address at the same port now gets `EADDRINUSE` instead of silently shadowing the live hub on loopback.
- Failed sentinel binds are logged as warnings instead of crashing the hub, so a process already shadowing the port does not prevent the live service from coming up — the warning surfaces the condition for the operator.
- `stop()` closes the main server and all sentinels in parallel.

## Background
Before this change, a wildcard `*:PORT` bind only reserves the port on addresses that are not yet specifically bound. A worker calling `listen("127.0.0.1", PORT)` succeeded, and BSD socket precedence routed loopback traffic to that more-specific bind. The hub remained alive on the wildcard, serving only non-loopback addresses, while the operator's browser at `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` saw the worker's app. This actually happened today on port 3000 — `wrangler pages dev --port 3000` from a clawso worktree shadowed the Meridian Hub UI on `127.0.0.1:3000`.

The companion fix in clawso (https://github.com/yzsnstotz/clawso/pull/431) changes the worker's default wrangler ports to `8788`/`8789` and documents a reserved-port policy. This Meridian-side fix is the defense-in-depth: even if a future tool ignores the policy, it cannot shadow the hub on loopback because the sentinels hold the port.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean.
- [x] Live hub is currently running with this change unbuilt; will be picked up on the next operator-initiated rebuild_restart.
- [ ] Post-merge, operator restarts the hub: confirm `Web Interface Server reserved loopback` log lines for `127.0.0.1` and `::1` appear, then attempt `python3 -m http.server 3000 --bind 127.0.0.1` and verify it fails with `Address already in use`.

## 무엇을 / 왜

`core-js` 런타임 폴리필 (`--runtime-polyfills`)에 대한 설명·사용법이 `guides/bundling.md` 와 `reference/options.md` 의 하위 섹션으로만 존재해서, 사이드바를 훑어보면 "core-js" 나 "polyfill" 항목이 안 보여 **문서가 없는 것처럼** 보였습니다 (사용자 피드백). 특히 `@babel/preset-env` 의 `useBuiltIns` + `core-js` 를 쓰던 Babel/Metro 사용자에게는 1st-class 관심사라 전용 페이지로 분리했습니다.

## 변경

- **신규** `guides/runtime-polyfills.md` (KO) + `en/guides/runtime-polyfills.md` (EN):
  - 문법 vs 런타임 API 구분 — `--target` 은 syntax (arrow → function 등), `--runtime-polyfills` 는 `Promise`/`Map`/`String.prototype.replaceAll`/`Array.prototype.at`/`structuredClone` 같은 **런타임 API**
  - 설치 (`bun add core-js core-js-compat` — optional dep)
  - 모드 표 (`off`/`auto`/`usage`/`entry`) + **`@babel/preset-env useBuiltIns` 대응** (`usage` ↔ `auto`, `entry` ↔ `{mode:"entry"}`, `false` ↔ `off`)
  - CLI 플래그 (`--runtime-polyfills` / `--runtime-target` / `--core-js`)
  - `runtimePolyfills` 설정 객체 필드 (`mode`/`provider`/`targets`/`coreJs`/`include`/`exclude`/`proposals`)
  - 실행 순서 (`polyfills` → runtime core-js prelude → `runBeforeMain` → entry)
  - 디버깅 (`ZNTC_DEBUG=runtime_polyfills` + `--profile=graph`)
  - cross-link
- **`astro.config.mjs`**: "번들러" 섹션에 "런타임 폴리필 (core-js)" / "Runtime Polyfills (core-js)" 항목 추가 (트리쉐이킹 ↔ manualChunks 사이).
- **`guides/bundling.md`** (KO/EN): 기존 "Runtime Polyfills (core-js)" 섹션 (~75줄) 을 짧은 요약 + 전용 가이드 포인터로 트림 — 내용 중복 제거, 단일 출처화.
- **`guides/babel-migration.md`** (KO/EN): 대응 매트릭스에 `@babel/preset-env { useBuiltIns: "usage", corejs }` → `runtimePolyfills: "auto"` 행 추가, "관련"/"See also" 에 가이드 링크. `@babel/preset-env` 행도 "(문법 다운레벨)" 로 명시.
- **`reference/options.md`** (KO/EN): `runtimePolyfills` 섹션 상단에 전용 가이드 포인터 (설정 객체 레퍼런스는 그대로 유지).

## 검증

- `cd documents && bun run build` ✅ — `starlight-links-validator` 통과. (처음엔 `/guides/...` 로 썼더니 fail — 이 사이트는 `/zntc/` base path 라 모든 internal link 가 `/zntc/...`, EN 은 `/zntc/en/...` 여야 함. 전부 수정.)
- `bun run fmt` / `bun run lint` ✅
- 빌드된 사이트 `documents/dist/` 에 `guides/runtime-polyfills/` + `en/guides/runtime-polyfills/` 페이지 생성 확인
