author: whilo
body:
## Summary

Removes the `has-scanless-base?` guard in `plan-rule-op` that routed any recursive rule whose base branch lacked an `:entity-group` / `:pattern-scan` op through `legacy/solve-rule`. Legacy can't evaluate recursive bodies that bind head vars through `:function` ops and then filter them with predicates — those queries raise `Cannot resolve any more clauses` or never terminate.

Two real shapes that hit this regression:

- **SQL `WITH RECURSIVE`**: anchors like `SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n+1 FROM t WHERE n < N` lower to a `[(identity 1) ?n]` base case. Surfaced via the SQL → Datalog translator in pg-datahike.
- **`[(ground […]) [?v ...]]` collection seeds**: rules whose entry point is a literal set rather than a scan.

The fixpoint executor already handles these: `execute-branch-plans` runs the base plan against an empty ctx, `legacy/bind-by-fn` produces a single-tuple Relation, and the recursive branch's `rule-lookup` ops feed off the accumulator as usual. Magic sets are silently skipped when `base-scan-attr` is nil (the existing `and magic-demand base-scan-attr …` check in `execute-recursive-rule`). The guard was redundant.

## Test plan

- [x] datahike `:clj-pss` suite under `DATAHIKE_QUERY_PLANNER=true`: 1510 tests, 7217 assertions, 0 failures
- [x] jobtech-taxonomy-api full suite under the patched datahike: 725 tests, 5416 assertions, 1 failure (timezone-only `mini-db-test` year boundary, unrelated)
- [x] jobtech-taxonomy-api's recursive `indirectly-replaced-by` rule (`replaced-concept-tracker-test/track-test`) — all sub-tests pass
- [x] End-to-end SQL `WITH RECURSIVE t(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n+1 FROM t WHERE n < 5) SELECT n FROM t` returns `{1,2,3,4,5}`
- [x] End-to-end SQL tree traversal with `depth+1` returns correct levels

author: carpenike
body:
Closes #113. Brings the frontend ESLint quality gate to parity with the Python ruff gate from PR #89.

## TL;DR

```
+ scripts/eslint_diff_check.py (360 LOC)  ← line-level diff-aware ESLint gate
± .pre-commit-config.yaml                  ← strip 'frontend/' prefix; treat exit code as advisory
± scripts/ci-quality-gate.sh               ← Stage 1 invokes both diff-checks; SKIP eslint-staged in pre-commit
± docs/code-quality-tools.md (+50 LOC)     ← documents the paired diff-check pattern
± .github/copilot-instructions.md          ← drops stale 'ZERO WARNINGS REQUIRED' claim
```

After this lands, frontend PRs no longer need `--admin` to merge.

## What was broken

### Bug 1: path-stripping

`.pre-commit-config.yaml`'s `eslint-staged` hook did:
```yaml
entry: bash -c 'cd frontend && npx eslint --fix -- "$@"' --
```

Pre-commit passes paths repo-relative (`frontend/src/foo.tsx`). After `cd frontend`, eslint looked for `frontend/frontend/src/foo.tsx` and exited 2 with "No files matching the pattern". This caused PR #110's CI failure and is why every frontend PR since #89 has needed `--admin`.

### Bug 2: no diff-awareness

Even after Bug 1, eslint reports errors on the WHOLE file. The frontend has 648 pre-existing legacy errors. Touching one line in any frontend file would have flooded the gate.

This is exactly the problem ruff had until `scripts/ruff_diff_check.py` introduced line-level diff-awareness in PR #89. Now the frontend has the same treatment.

## What this PR adds

### `scripts/eslint_diff_check.py` (new, 360 LOC)

Mirror of `scripts/ruff_diff_check.py`:

| Feature | Behavior |
|---------|----------|
| Default base ref | `origin/main` |
| Diff range | three-dot (`A...HEAD`); falls back to two-dot on shallow clones |
| File scope | `frontend/.*\.(js\|jsx\|ts\|tsx)$`; skips node_modules / dist / coverage |
| Tool invocation | `npx eslint --format=json --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern` from `frontend/` with stripped paths |
| Blocking | NEW errors (severity 2) |
| Advisory | NEW warnings (severity 1) — printed but exit 0 unless `--warnings-fail` |
| Footer | `(N legacy error(s) + M legacy warning(s) on unchanged lines were ignored.)` |
| Exit codes | 0 = pass / 1 = new errors / 2 = tooling failure |

The script intentionally duplicates ~80 LOC of diff-parsing helpers from `ruff_diff_check.py` rather than factoring them into a shared module. Each script is a standalone tool that should not depend on the other being installed/working — same tradeoff the existing ruff script makes.

### `.pre-commit-config.yaml`

The `eslint-staged` hook now:
- Strips the `frontend/` prefix from each arg (fixes Bug 1).
- Treats eslint's exit code as advisory (`|| true`) — applying `--fix` is the goal; blocking on legacy errors is not.

This mirrors the existing Python pattern: `ruff format` is a file-level autofix in pre-commit, and `ruff_diff_check.py` is the diff-aware gate in CI.

### `scripts/ci-quality-gate.sh`

Stage 1 now also runs `scripts/eslint_diff_check.py`. The pre-commit invocation in Stage 1 SKIPs both `ruff` and `eslint-staged` (now CI-gate's job).

### Documentation

- `docs/code-quality-tools.md` — new "Diff-Aware Quality Gates" section + a "Frontend Code Quality Tools" subsection with the right `npm` commands.
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md` — replaced the stale "ESLint - ZERO WARNINGS REQUIRED" claim (the project has 1496 warnings) with the accurate description of the pragmatic-mode gate.

## Verification (three test cases)

```bash
# 1. PR #110's actual diff (should pass — that's the point):
$ python3 scripts/eslint_diff_check.py origin/main
✅ No NEW ESLint errors on changed lines (3 file(s) checked).
   (28 legacy error(s) + 39 legacy warning(s) on unchanged lines were ignored.)
exit=0

# 2. Synthetic new error (added a security/detect-object-injection violation):
$ python3 scripts/eslint_diff_check.py origin/main
❌ 2 NEW ESLint error(s) on lines added/changed in this PR:
Errors:
  frontend/src/pages/can-sniffer.tsx:660:12: @typescript-eslint/consistent-indexed-object-style ...
  frontend/src/pages/can-sniffer.tsx:662:13: security/detect-object-injection ...
exit=1

# 3. No frontend changes at all (no-op):
$ python3 scripts/eslint_diff_check.py origin/main
No changed frontend files vs origin/main — nothing to check.
exit=0
```

Bash + YAML + Python syntax all validate.

## What this PR does NOT do

- Does NOT fix any of the 648 pre-existing eslint errors. That's the whole point of pragmatic mode — those errors stay until someone touches their lines, and the diff-check forces them to be fixed-or-acknowledged.
- Does NOT add an ESLint baseline counter (the way pyright has `EXPECTED_PYRIGHT_ERRORS`). Could be added later; not needed for this PR's goal. #107 is the umbrella issue for ratcheting, and it can include ESLint when picked up.
- Does NOT touch the `npm run typecheck` gate that PR #110 already ratcheted to 0; this is a separate, parallel gate.

## Side effect on PR #110

Once both this PR and #110 land, PR #110's CI will pass on its own. No more `--admin` for routine frontend PRs.

## Tracker
Updates checkbox in #108.

author: timlichtenberg
body:
## Description

Three bundled changes on this branch:

1. **Lower coverage ceiling 95→90**: 95% has been unrealistically tight for this ecosystem. Sister repos have flapped in the 94.9–95.6 % band on identical source under xdist parallelism. The new 90% ceiling leaves several pp of permanent headroom. Updates `pyproject.toml [tool.coverage.report] fail_under = 90` (was 95), `[tool.coverage.run] source = ["aragog"]` (was `["src/aragog"]`) so the cov target is install-mode-agnostic. Workflow `--cov=aragog --cov-fail-under=90`. `.codecov.yml coverage.range: "70...90"` so the Codecov badge maxes bright green at 90%. Ratchet-guard floor anchored at `min(base, 90.0)`.

2. **Migrate from Poetry to setuptools-scm**: matches the Zalmoxis 26.05.10 release scheme. `[project] dynamic = ["version"]` replaces the hand-edited `version = "26.05.10"`; added `[tool.setuptools_scm] version_file = "src/aragog/_version.py"`. `src/aragog/__init__.py` reads `_version.py` with a `0.0.0.dev0` fallback (marked `# pragma: no cover - source-checkout fallback before setuptools-scm runs`). Rewrote `publish.yaml` from Poetry to `python -m build` with `fetch-depth: 0` and `setuptools-scm>=8`. Bumped `actions/checkout@v4 → @v5` in `publish.yaml` and `publish-test-badges.yml` ahead of the Node 20 deprecation on 2026-06-02. Added `docs/How-to/releasing.md` (matching CALLIOPE and Zalmoxis) and wired it into `mkdocs.yml` so contributors have a single page describing the tag-driven flow.

3. **Docs**: `CLAUDE.md` previously claimed "85% Codecov floor" — fixed to "90% PROTEUS-ecosystem ceiling". Also rewrote the `__version__` rule from "should match pyproject.toml" to the setuptools-scm reality. Tightened the EntropySolver-re-export wording so the new top-level version-shim import is not confused with the circular-import workaround. Added a PR template matching CALLIOPE/Zalmoxis convention.

- Local `pytest -m unit -o "addopts="`: full suite passes (~2 min wall).

author: elderalvesf
body:
## Problem

After login succeeds (`home_screen` visible), all specs were failing in `beforeEach` because `nav_appointments` / `nav_home` / etc. could not be found within the 5-second timeout.

Root cause: two compounding issues:
1. **Keyboard still visible** — `mobile: type` leaves the IME open, and `hideKeyboard()` was failing silently. Clicking `btn_entrar` does not reliably dismiss the IME in Compose with `enableEdgeToEdge()`, so the keyboard animation was still running when the tests started navigating. The bottom `NavigationBar` may be considered "not displayed" while the keyboard overlaps it.
2. **isTopLevel race** — after Firebase auth transitions `authState` to `Authenticated`, Compose re-renders `AppNavigation` with a fresh `navController`. The `NavigationBar` is only rendered when `isTopLevel = true`, which flips once `NavHost` sets the initial back-stack entry. The `home_screen` LazyColumn can become accessible one frame before the bar appears.

## Fix

- Press `KEYCODE_ENTER` (66) after typing the password so the IME is dismissed cleanly via the standard IME action before tapping the login button.
- After `home_screen` appears, also `waitForDisplayed` on `nav_home` (10 s) so the `before` hook only returns once the bottom navigation bar is confirmed visible.
- Increase `NavigationHelper` `waitForDisplayed` timeouts 5 s → 15 s as an extra safety margin on all navigation actions.

GitHub Pages caches CSS and JS files, so browsers keep serving old versions even after new code is deployed. This caused users to see old layouts and missing fixes after merges.

author: farisalkr
body:
## Summary

Replaces the existing cursor ink-stroke trail with a sequential Arabic letter trail. As the cursor moves, the letters of **"إرم 366 الإخبارية"** are stamped one at a time at the cursor position, in order, looping back to the first letter after the last. Letters fade out behind the cursor.

Two commits on `feat/arabic-letter-cursor`:

### Commit 1 — `feat(cursor): add Amiri Arabic display font for letter cursor`
- Loads **Amiri** (Naskh-style classical Arabic display face) via `next/font/google` in `src/app/(frontend)/layout.tsx`.
- `preload: false`, `subsets: ['arabic']`, single `weight: ['700']` to keep the bundle small. The trail is desktop-only and gated by 4 separate switches — there's no reason to make every mobile visitor pay for the font on LCP.
- Exposes the font via a `--font-cursor-arabic` CSS variable + an `.iram-cursor-letter-trail` class. The canvas reads `getComputedStyle(canvas).fontFamily` to build `ctx.font`, because canvas font strings don't resolve CSS variables.

### Commit 2 — `feat(cursor): replace ink trail with sequential Arabic letter trail`
Rewrites `src/components/CursorInk.tsx`. The filename and component name are deliberately preserved — the admin toggle (`siteSettings.signatureUi.enableCursorInk`) and the env flag (`NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_CURSOR_INK`) both reference this name, and renaming would require a Payload schema migration just to relabel a boolean. Top-of-file comment now explains the historical name.

**Mechanics**:
- `LETTERS = Array.from('إرم 366 الإخبارية')` — code-point safe split. The Amiri font handles Arabic contextual shaping at render time.
- Every `STAMP_DISTANCE_PX = 60` of *accumulated cursor travel* we push a stamp `{ char, x, y, age }` at the current pointer position and advance an unbounded `letterIndex` (modulo `LETTERS.length` when read). Distance-based stamping gives a constant visual rhythm regardless of cursor speed.
- Whitespace glyphs advance the index but aren't pushed — avoids visually-empty gaps.
- Ring buffer capped at `MAX_STAMPS = 20`.
- Each frame: clear → draw stamps with `alpha = 1 - age/MAX_AGE` → age each stamp → splice dead ones (age > `MAX_AGE = 60` frames ≈ 1 s @ 60 fps). Draw-before-age so newly-pushed stamps paint at full alpha on their first frame.
- **Performance**: early-exit when `stamps.length === 0`. `fillText` is meaningfully more expensive than the old per-segment strokes, and the trail is empty most of the time (idle pages, readers paused on text). Without this the rAF loop would burn CPU drawing transparent canvases forever.
- Idle handling: when the gap between two pointermove events exceeds `IDLE_MS_TO_STOP_STAMPING = 500 ms` we reset the sample anchor and the accumulator. `letterIndex` is intentionally **not** reset — the phrase resumes from where it left off when the user moves again.

**Rendering**:
- 700 weight, 28 px, Amiri.
- Color `#c8964a` (the warm ochre from the previous implementation).
- `textAlign: center` + `textBaseline: middle` → letters center on the cursor.
- Subtle drop shadow `rgba(0,0,0,0.15)` blur 4 for legibility on mixed backgrounds.

**Preserved safeguards (all unchanged):**
- The existing `enableCursorInk` admin toggle still controls this component — no new toggle introduced.
- The `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_CURSOR_INK` build-time env flag still gates the whole feature.
- Touch detection (`pointer: coarse`), `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, and `/admin` route all early-return.
- `has-pen-cursor` body class still added/removed in lockstep so the pen-shaped CSS cursor rides above the letter trail.
- `visualViewport` zoom-aware sizing + resize/scroll listeners from PR #15 intact.
- Full buffer clear on `mouseleave` / `blur` so the trail doesn't persist as a stale snapshot on tab re-entry.

## Caveat
This is a **creative visual feature** that may need 1–2 tuning passes after deploy. Likely tuning candidates:
- `STAMP_DISTANCE_PX` (currently 60 — too dense or too sparse?)
- `FONT_SIZE_PX` (currently 28 — too big or too small on retina?)
- `MAX_AGE` (currently 60 frames ≈ 1 s — letters fade too fast or linger too long?)
- `COLOR` (currently `#c8964a` — adjust for contrast over the cream body / navy header / dark footer?)

I haven't been able to click-test in a browser myself — please verify the trail behavior on the deploy and tell me what to tune.

## Test plan
- [ ] Move the mouse slowly across the homepage; letters appear one at a time, in order, spelling out **إرم 366 الإخبارية**.
- [ ] Move fast across the page; the stream of letters still appears in order (no skipping).
- [ ] Stop moving; existing letters fade out, no new letters appear, no CPU spike on the empty page.
- [ ] Resume movement after a pause; letters resume from where the sequence left off.
- [ ] Ctrl+- zoom out and continue moving; letters still render correctly at the new viewport size.
- [ ] `/admin` route: no trail (Payload UI's own cursor is preserved).
- [ ] Mobile / touch device: no trail (no canvas mounted).

**Do not merge yet** — eyeball on the live deploy first.

body:
### What

Adds two optional constructor parameters to `WarmTransferTask`:

- **`dtmf: str | None`** — DTMF tones to send once the human agent's call is answered, e.g. to dial an extension or navigate an IVR menu (`"1234#"`, or `"wwww1234#"` to pause ~2s first). Passed through to `CreateSIPParticipantRequest.dtmf`.
- **`ringing_timeout: float | None`** — seconds to wait for the human agent to answer before giving up; passed through to `CreateSIPParticipantRequest.ringing_timeout` (as a protobuf `Duration`). On timeout the task completes with a `ToolError` and the caller conversation resumes.

Also adds usage hints to `examples/warm-transfer/warm_transfer.py` and a changeset.

### Why

`WarmTransferTask` dials the human agent via `CreateSIPParticipantRequest` inside `_dial_human_agent`, but never exposed the request's `dtmf` / `ringing_timeout` fields. Warm-transferring to a destination behind an extension or IVR (common for PBX/desk-phone transfers), or bounding the ring time before falling back to the caller, currently requires subclassing the task and copy-pasting all of `_dial_human_agent` just to set those fields — brittle against upstream changes to that method.

Per @davidzhao's note on #5716, scoped to `dtmf` + `ringing_timeout`; happy to expose more `CreateSIPParticipantRequest` fields (`max_call_duration`, `play_dialtone`, `krisp_enabled`, `media_encryption`, …) in a follow-up if wanted.

Closes #5716

- `ruff format` / `ruff check` — pass
- `python scripts/check_types.py` — pass

## Summary

- Versioned a GitHub ruleset at `.github/rulesets/protect-main.json` that targets the default branch with `deletion` and `non_fast_forward` rules — exactly what [YAU-26](https://linear.app/yaubi/issue/YAU-26/protect-main-branch-from-force-pushing-or-deletion) calls for, nothing more.
- Added a `sync-rulesets` workflow that upserts every JSON file under `.github/rulesets/` via the Rulesets API (idempotent: PUT if a ruleset with the same name already exists, POST otherwise). Triggered on push to `main` when `.github/rulesets/**` changes, and via `workflow_dispatch`.
- The existing `update-calendar` workflow does plain fast-forward pushes, so these rules will not affect its monthly commit.

## Auth note

The Rulesets API needs the `administration` permission. The workflow grants `administration: write` to `GITHUB_TOKEN`. If that returns `403 Resource not accessible by integration` on first run, the fallback is a fine-grained PAT with `Administration: read/write` stored as `RULESET_SYNC_TOKEN`, and switch the workflow's `GH_TOKEN` env to that secret.

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge this PR (the merge commit will trigger `sync-rulesets` via the path filter — alternatively run `gh workflow run sync-rulesets.yml --ref main`).
- [ ] Confirm the workflow run succeeds. If it fails with 403, switch to the PAT fallback.
- [ ] `gh api repos/YoannAubineau/bonne-fete-fr/rulesets --jq '.[] | {name, enforcement, target}'` reports the active ruleset.
- [ ] `gh api repos/YoannAubineau/bonne-fete-fr/rules/branches/main --jq '[.[].type] | sort'` returns `["deletion","non_fast_forward"]`.
- [ ] `git push --force-with-lease origin main` is rejected by the remote.
- [ ] `git push origin --delete main` is rejected by the remote.
- [ ] The next scheduled `update-calendar` run still pushes its commit to `main` successfully.

$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

- Upgrades `python_version` from `3.9` to `3.10` in `Pipfile` and `Pipfile.lock`
- Fixes two high-severity urllib3 CVEs (GHSA-qccp-gfcp-xxvc, GHSA-mf9v-mfxr-j63j) by making the lock file consistent with the already-pinned urllib3 2.7.0
- Corrects the `_meta.hash`, `_meta.requires.python_version`, and urllib3 `markers` fields in `Pipfile.lock`

## Root cause

urllib3 2.7.0 (which fixes both CVEs) requires **Python >= 3.10**, but the Pipfile declared `python_version = "3.9"`. This is why dependabot alert #46 could not be resolved automatically — pipenv correctly refused to pin an incompatible version. The manual patch in `bada372` pinned 2.7.0 in the lock file without updating the Python requirement, leaving the lock file internally inconsistent.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `Pipfile` | `python_version = "3.9"` → `"3.10"` |
| `Pipfile.lock` `_meta.hash.sha256` | recomputed for new Pipfile |
| `Pipfile.lock` `_meta.requires.python_version` | `"3.9"` → `"3.10"` |
| `Pipfile.lock` urllib3 `markers` | `python_version >= '3.9'` → `python_version >= '3.10'` |

author: gengyveusa
body:
## Summary

First of three PRs in the **v0.6.x `moc-add` slice** per [ADR-017 D6](https://github.com/Gengyveusa/obsidian-claude-conduit/blob/main/docs/2026-05-11-adr-017-phase-5-plan.md#d6--rollout-slicing). Stand-alone helpers — no production wiring yet. PR 2 ships the classifier; PR 3 wires it in and ships v0.6.2.

## What's in

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/organization/MocDetection.ts` | Pure helpers: `looksLikeMoc(content): boolean` + `analyzeMocShape(content): MocShapeMetrics`. Detection is shape-based per ADR-017 D6 — heading + ≥3 wikilink bullets + link density ≥ 0.3. Frontmatter stripped before measurement. |
| `src/organization/MocDiscovery.ts` | Service that scans configured `mocFolders`, runs the shape heuristic, returns `MocCandidate` list. Uses `adapter.listAllMarkdown()` + prefix filter (cheap; per ADR-015). Sorted by wikilink count desc so denser MOCs lead the eventual classifier prompt. |

## Design notes

- **Shape-based, not filename- or frontmatter-based.** Users don't have to tag MOCs explicitly. A `# Decisions\n- [[ADR-001]]\n- [[ADR-002]]\n- [[ADR-003]]` file is recognized regardless of name.
- **Density threshold (≥30%)** prevents false positives on prose-heavy notes that happen to mention a few wikilinks inline (e.g., a meeting note with a couple of `[[Pipeline_State]]` mentions).
- **`mocFolders === []` short-circuits to `[]`** — lets users disable moc-add entirely by clearing the setting.
- **Best-effort discovery** — files that fail to read are silently skipped (don't crash the watcher loop on a transient I/O bump).

## Tests (22 new; 534 total)

| Suite | Cases | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| `MocDetection.spec.ts` | 14 | All three bullet styles (-, *, numbered). Bullets with trailing prose. Frontmatter ignored. Aliased wikilinks. Rejects: no heading, <3 wikilink bullets, density < 30%, prose notes with inline links. Metrics: firstHeading extraction, null heading, density rounding, blank-line handling. |
| `MocDiscovery.spec.ts` | 8 | Empty mocFolders short-circuit. No-MOC case. Found candidates filtered to in-folder. Multi-folder support. Trailing-slash normalization. Sort by density desc. Silent skip on read failure. Files outside scope excluded. |

## Gates

- `npm run typecheck` clean
- `npm run lint` clean
- `npm test` — **534/534 pass** (+22 new)
- (No build needed — no production wiring yet.)

## What's next

- **PR 2** (v0.6.x): `MocAddClassifier` — single LLM call that takes a note + the discovered MOC candidates and returns the best match (or null = no fit). Sonnet default, mirrors `OrganizationClassifier`'s shape.
- **PR 3** (v0.6.x ship as v0.6.2): integrate moc-add into the watcher, wire the Apply path in `SuggestionsView` to call `link_notes`, expose the `organizationMocFolders` setting, end-to-end smoke.

## Related

- [ADR-017 D3](https://github.com/Gengyveusa/obsidian-claude-conduit/blob/main/docs/2026-05-11-adr-017-phase-5-plan.md#d3--suggestion-types-for-v06x) — `moc-add` suggestion type spec.
- [ADR-017 D6](https://github.com/Gengyveusa/obsidian-claude-conduit/blob/main/docs/2026-05-11-adr-017-phase-5-plan.md#d6--rollout-slicing) — v0.6.x slice this PR opens.

body:
This pull request introduces several improvements and new features to the Blocks Network SDK, CLI, and release workflows. The most notable changes include the addition of new GitHub Actions workflows for publishing to npm and Artifactory, expanded platform support for CLI releases, updated documentation and licensing, enhanced authentication flows in the CLI, and a new comprehensive changelog.

**Release and Packaging Improvements:**

* Added `.github/workflows/mcp-npm-publish.yaml` to automate publishing the MCP Server to the public npm registry when tags matching `mcp-npm-v*` are pushed.
* Added `.github/workflows/mcp-sdk-publish.yaml` for publishing the MCP Server to Artifactory on tags matching `mcp-v*`.
* Expanded CLI cross-compilation to include FreeBSD and OpenBSD (amd64 and arm64) in `cli/.goreleaser.yaml` and updated release instructions in `RELEASING.md` to clarify which platforms are published to npm and which are distributed via GitHub Releases. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-753cc4c452735002ee9b8c2feb79f048956800076a027594557aa230d428d82dR23-R24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-87d6a57a759f2386bf9caf5309b9aa0b9ff0ca70f5e38696e114a1ccdb0e785dL74-R97)

**Documentation and Licensing:**

* Introduced a new `cli/LICENSE` file with a custom Blocks Network SDK license agreement.
* Added a detailed `CHANGELOG.md` covering the Node SDK, Python SDK, and CLI, summarizing all notable changes and release history.
* Updated `cli/README.md` to document new authentication commands, installation options for BSD platforms, and improved local development instructions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a60fd8fcc968f85dd50305193d1af8e94118afb7439f90c07bb434acd3490fabL13-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a60fd8fcc968f85dd50305193d1af8e94118afb7439f90c07bb434acd3490fabL49-R71) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a60fd8fcc968f85dd50305193d1af8e94118afb7439f90c07bb434acd3490fabR87)

**CLI Authentication and Usability:**

* Changed the `blocks publish` command to require prior authentication with `blocks login` or an explicit `--api-key`, improving error messages and credential handling. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0f6d368f13ebfd848bd78ae1405e1fa2aecc35fbfff7ae9b1faecdb190f0566cL55-L74) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0f6d368f13ebfd848bd78ae1405e1fa2aecc35fbfff7ae9b1faecdb190f0566cR235-R265)
* Improved user guidance in CLI messages and help text, and updated onboarding instructions for new agent projects. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1d8fe5889cb8e0e5a24f1fe9f788c4f2b1f843be25c23075fda78f87d2c1502fL140-R141) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a3bbb588aa7b36bffdfc655b38243e697ec6fd9abda92a19e7afe5b04d5b9a48L77-R77)
* Enhanced test coverage for publishing with API keys, ensuring correct Authorization header usage. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0d21e9b65e84bbcad876b0ceafb8aa0a1c3dc198efbe0f94ce2bbef3fdbe6dafL284-R284) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0d21e9b65e84bbcad876b0ceafb8aa0a1c3dc198efbe0f94ce2bbef3fdbe6dafL301-R309) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0d21e9b65e84bbcad876b0ceafb8aa0a1c3dc198efbe0f94ce2bbef3fdbe6dafL331-R337)

These changes collectively improve the release process, platform support, documentation quality, and user experience for both developers and end-users of the Blocks Network SDK and CLI.

## Summary

Migrates fast-data-entry-app's test runner from jest to vitest, aligning it with the patterns adopted across the rest of the O3 apps.

Changes:
- Replace `jest`, `@swc/jest`, `jest-cli`, `jest-environment-jsdom`, `@types/jest`, and `@types/testing-library__jest-dom` with `vitest`, `@vitest/coverage-v8`, `jsdom`, and `cross-env`. Bump `@testing-library/dom` (7.x to 10.x), `@testing-library/jest-dom` (5.x to 6.x), and `@testing-library/react` (13.x to 16.x) so the `/vitest` subpath is available.
- Add `vitest.config.ts`: `jsdom` environment, `.scss`/`.css` aliased to `identity-obj-proxy` via the anchored `^.*\.s?css$` regex, `@openmrs/esm-framework` aliased to its mock, `react-i18next` aliased to the local `__mocks__` file, and `fakeTimers.toFake` limited so it does not break React's scheduler.
- Replace `src/setup-tests.ts`'s `'@testing-library/jest-dom/extend-expect'` import with `'@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest'` and register `afterEach(cleanup)`.
- Convert the eleven test files to the vitest API: explicit imports for `describe`/`expect`/`it`/`vi` (plus `beforeEach`/`afterEach`/`type Mock`/`type MockedFunction` where used), `jest.*` swapped for `vi.*`. One `vi.mock(name, () => vi.fn())` factory wrapped in `{ default: vi.fn() }` for vitest's module-object shape requirement.

journalEntry-type embedded items (per-actor notes, no compendium

body:
## Resumen

Limpieza de artefactos de firma de Play Store que quedaron commiteados accidentalmente en el working tree de `develop`:

- `pepk.jar` (2.1 MB) — binario público de Google, no debe versionarse
- `output.zip` (3 KB) — contiene `encryptedPrivateKey` + `certificate.pem`, artefacto del proceso PEPK
- `private_key 2` (1.7 KB) — otro `encryptedPrivateKey` duplicado

## Análisis de severidad

**No hay leak crítico explotable.** Los blobs son la versión cifrada con la public key de Google (solo Google puede descifrar) + el certificado público (que ya se distribuye con cada APK firmado). Las claves reales de firma siguen viviendo fuera del repo (`frontend/mobile/key`, `frontend/mobile/private_key.pepk` según CLAUDE.md, sección "Claves Android pendientes de reubicar").

## Acciones tomadas

- [x] Borrar los 3 archivos del working tree
- [x] Reforzar `.gitignore` con `pepk.jar`, `private_key*`, `output.zip`, `certificate.pem`
- [x] Consolidar la sección duplicada de "Signing keystores" en `.gitignore`

## Lo que NO se hizo (por decisión, no por descuido)

- **No se reescribió historia git** (`git filter-repo` / force-push). Razones:
  1. No hay leak explotable que justifique el blast radius
  2. `develop` está protegida; force-push afectaría muchos PRs activos
  3. CLAUDE.md prohíbe `git push --force` a ramas compartidas
- **No se rotan claves de firma de Play Console** — no es necesario (blob cifrado).

## Cómo testear

- [ ] Verificar que `npm install --legacy-peer-deps` sigue funcionando
- [ ] Verificar que `npm run build` produce el bundle correctamente
- [ ] Confirmar que el `.gitignore` actualizado no rompe otros workflows

## Requiere release a Play Store

No — cambio puramente de housekeeping del repo, no toca código Angular ni nativo.

## Riesgo

Bajo. Si alguien tenía esos archivos como referencia local, no se ven afectados (no se borraron del filesystem fuera del repo). Si se necesitan regenerar para subir una nueva key a Play Console, se puede correr `pepk.jar` localmente y mantener el output fuera del repo.

Contexto: este PR salió de una auditoría disparada por el ataque Mini Shai-Hulud al ecosistema npm (11-may-2026). `frc-mobile` resultó limpio de IoCs del worm; estos archivos fueron un hallazgo lateral.

author: enejb
body:
## Summary

Adds a single read-only ability to the `automattic/jetpack-connection` package so AI agents can answer "is this site connected?" through the standard `wp-abilities/v1` REST surface.

Slug registered:

- `jetpack/get-connection-status` — site-level state as `{ site_connected, user_connected, master_user, blog_id, registration_url, connection_version }`. Zero-arg. Read-only. Idempotent.
  - `site_connected` — true when the site has a blog id and a blog token.
  - `user_connected` — true when at least one user has linked their WordPress.com account.
  - `master_user` — local user id of the connection owner, or null when there is no owner.
  - `blog_id` — WordPress.com site id, or null when the site has not been registered.
  - `registration_url` — wp-admin URL the site owner should visit to register the site when `site_connected` is false; null once connected.
  - `connection_version` — running Jetpack Connection package version.

The ability extends `Automattic\Jetpack\WP_Abilities\Registrar`, lives in category `jetpack` (label "Jetpack"), is gated behind the package-wide `jetpack_wp_abilities_enabled` filter (default `false`), and uses `Manager::is_connected()` / `Manager::has_connected_user()` rather than raw option reads. Authenticated users only — anonymous requests are denied by an `is_user_logged_in()` permission callback (no `WP_Error` payload, the Abilities API turns that into a 401 itself).

A current-user variant (`get-current-user-connection`) and writes (registering, disconnecting, transferring ownership) are deliberately deferred to a follow-up PR.

## Wiring scope

Registration is wired from the Jetpack plugin (`class.jetpack.php`) — **not** from the Connection package's `actions.php`. That intentionally scopes the ability to sites running the Jetpack plugin for now; connection-only consumers (Boost, Protect, Search, Backup, Social, VideoPress, …) do **not** register it yet. Broadening the wiring to the package's `actions.php` is the deferred follow-up.

`automattic/jetpack-wp-abilities` was added to the Connection package's `require-dev` so the test suite can resolve `Registrar`; runtime resolution still comes from the host plugin. The composer.lock churn across consumer plugins is just the auto-regenerated lock files picking up that dev-only require.

## Rollout plan reference

Maps to §4.2 (package-backed abilities live in their package) of the Abilities Everywhere rollout plan. Cross-consumer auto-wiring via the package's `actions.php` (§4.5) is intentionally deferred.

## Test plan

- [x] `composer phpunit -- --filter Connection_Abilities_Test` passes locally (13 tests).
- [x] Test coverage:
  - Registrar wiring: gate filter off registers nothing; gate filter on hooks both lifecycle actions; per-slug `jetpack_wp_abilities_should_register` filter short-circuits registration; category is auto-injected onto each registered ability.
  - Abstract getters: category slug (`jetpack`); category definition (label + description); abilities map lists the single read ability; no spec hard-codes a category; every spec declares annotations, permission_callback, and execute_callback.
  - Permission callback: anonymous denied; logged-in allowed.
  - Execute happy paths for both disconnected and connected states, with a `Connection_Manager` stub injected via the new `jetpack_connection_abilities_manager` filter.
- [x] `phpcs` clean on the new/changed files using the repo `.phpcs.xml.dist` ruleset.
- [x] `changelogger validate` exits 0. Changelog entries: `added` on the Connection package, `enhancement` on the Jetpack plugin, and `patch` / `changed` ("Updated package dependencies.") on the other plugins whose composer.lock files picked up the new dev require.
- [ ] On a running WP site with `add_filter( 'jetpack_wp_abilities_enabled', '__return_true' )`, confirm the slug shows up via `wp_get_abilities()` and `/wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/abilities`, and that the payload matches expectations for both a connected and a disconnected site.

## Summary

Closes the M2.1 public-readiness loop by combining three pieces:

1. **3 new source packets** (HBM / cooling / passive components) to close the remaining component-layer gaps the user flagged in EP659.
2. **New analysis-reasoning rule** + template upgrade after the user pointed out the previous article was fact aggregation rather than reasoning. The rule requires every observation to walk Observation → Mechanism → Implication → Counter.
3. **Article rewrite** of sections 2/3/layers using the new reasoning frame. Section 1 (CPU) unchanged (user confirmed it reads well).

## Why a new reasoning rule

Existing rules covered tone (`content-voice-raw-research`) and claim classification (`source-tutor-reading`) but nothing required causal reasoning between facts. The voice rule actively prohibits institutional phrasing like `底層原因`, which was being mis-applied as "skip the mechanism entirely". The new rule sits between source-tutor (classification) and content-voice (tone) and governs reasoning structure.

## Commits

1. `feat(sources): add HBM / cooling / passive component source packets`
2. `feat(rules): add analysis-reasoning rule (observation → mechanism → implication)`
3. `feat(template): require Evidence + Reasoning structure in internal-article template`
4. `feat(article): rewrite sections 2/3/layers with reasoning frame + integrate v2 Intel + 3 new layers`

## Specific Rewrites in Sections 2/3/Layers

- **Section 2 (ASIC / MediaTek)**: replaced "需要小心" with explicit ASIC-exists mechanism (hyperscaler vs NVIDIA margin) + 4 concrete MediaTek-specific risks (track record, subsystem vs main chip, expectation reset, price-in).
- **Section 3 HBM**: unpacked "memory wall + 4-layer manufacturing bottleneck → allocation game". Three DRAM houses (Samsung / SK Hynix / Micron) positioned separately.
- **Section 3 Cooling**: unpacked "GPU power 700W ceiling → liquid cooling becomes necessary BOM, not optional".
- **Section 3 Passive**: unpacked "AI server capacitor density 2-3x → high-end MLCC manufacturing cycle 2-3 years → price + lead time pressure". Retained DigiTimes single-publisher caveat.
- **Layer section**: explained why Apple finds Intel (TSMC oversubscribed, not Intel independently strong), why Google diversifies to Marvell (supply-driven, not strategic), why CHIPS Act is floor not trigger (capex vs operating profit).

## Article public_status

`pending-scenario-and-human-edit` — remaining gates before public release are scenario-analyzer run, final human edit, plus passive-component evidence chain cross-publisher check and 信昌電 source verification.

## Bug que reportou

Mergeou o #254 mas não apareceu nada. Achei o motivo.

## Root cause

Em `src/app/(authed)/audiovisual/page.tsx:123`:

```ts
<PendenteEntregaAba
  ...
  canDeliver={isVideomaker}   // ← só videomaker passa essa prop como true
  clientes={clientes}
/>
```

`isVideomaker = user.role === "videomaker"`. Como você (adm/sócio/coord) **não é videomaker**, `canDeliver=false` → nenhum dos botões (nem upload, nem "Entregue") renderiza.

A server action `markCapturaEntregueRapidoAction` que adicionei no #254 JÁ permitia adm/socio/audiovisual_chefe/coordenador desde o começo. Mas a UI nunca expunha o botão pra eles.

`PendenteEntregaAba` ganhou **prop separada** `canQuickMark`:

| Prop | Quando true | O que mostra |
|---|---|---|
| `canDeliver` | só videomaker | ícone 📤 Upload (form completo com 7 ratings) |
| `canQuickMark` | videomaker + adm/socio/coord/audiovisual_chefe/assessor | botão verde "✓ Entregue" (modo rápido) |

Em `audiovisual/page.tsx`:
```ts
canDeliver={isVideomaker}
canQuickMark={isVideomaker || ROLES_GESTAO.includes(user.role)}
```

`ROLES_GESTAO` já existia no arquivo: `["audiovisual_chefe", "coordenador", "assessor", "adm", "socio"]`.

| Role | Vê na lista | Botões |

| audiovisual_chefe | todos | ✓ Entregue |
| coordenador | todos | ✓ Entregue |

body:
## Summary

- **Vote status indicator**: Off-chain proposals now surface whether the current user has already voted — fetched from the API on load and updated optimistically immediately after submission
- **Dynamic button label**: Vote button changes from "Cast your vote" to "Change your vote" (both desktop header and mobile bottom bar) when the user has already voted on an ongoing proposal
- **Modal copy fix**: Corrected inaccurate description "cannot change your vote later" → "Your vote can be updated until the proposal closes."; modal title also changes to "Change Your Vote" on re-vote
- **Display lag eliminated**: Removed `window.location.reload()` after vote submission; UI reflects the new voted state immediately via optimistic local state

## Approach

Three files changed, all in `apps/dashboard`:

1. **`OffchainVotingModal.tsx`** — Added `hasVoted` and `onVoteSuccess(voteLabel)` props; fixed description copy; changed title dynamically; removed page reload; computes and returns a human-readable vote label to the parent on success.

2. **`ProposalSection.tsx`** — Added `useGetOffchainVotesByProposalIdQuery` filtered by the connected address to check if the user has previously voted; maintains `localOffchainVoteLabel` state that is set immediately on `onVoteSuccess` (optimistic); derives `offchainHasVoted` and `offchainVoteLabel` from whichever is available first (local state or API); passes both down to `ProposalHeader` and `MobileBottomBar`.

3. **`ProposalHeader.tsx`** — `ProposalHeaderAction` now accepts `offchainHasVoted` and `offchainVoteLabel` props; when an off-chain vote is detected, renders an `OffchainVotedBadge` ("You voted [Choice]") plus a "Change your vote" button (if ongoing), instead of always showing "Cast your vote". `MobileBottomBar` mirrors the same logic.

## Files changed and why

| File | Why |
|---|---|
| `OffchainVotingModal.tsx` | Fix copy, dynamic title, remove page reload, expose vote result via callback |
| `ProposalSection.tsx` | Fetch user vote from API, maintain optimistic state, wire new props to children |
| `ProposalHeader.tsx` | Display off-chain vote badge and dynamic button label in desktop header and mobile bar |

## Assumptions I made

- The Snapshot API returns votes with `choice` as a 1-indexed string array (e.g., `["1"]` = first choice). The label is derived as `choices[Number(choice[0]) - 1]`.
- For multi-choice proposals (approval, ranked-choice, weighted, quadratic), the vote label is computed in the modal at submission time and passed back — subsequent page loads will show the primary choice from the API.
- Showing a generic "You voted" badge without a specific label when the label can't be resolved (e.g., index out of bounds) is acceptable.
- The optimistic local state is sufficient for the current session; refreshing the page will re-fetch from the API, which should have indexed the vote by then.

## What I did NOT do

- Did not modify the on-chain voting path — changes are strictly isolated to the off-chain / Snapshot flow.
- Did not add new test files or modify existing ones.
- Did not touch API, indexer, gateway, or any non-dashboard packages.
- Did not handle the edge case where Snapshot's hub accepts the vote but the anticapture API hasn't indexed it yet on page refresh — the display lag fix is client-side only.

## Open questions for review

1. Should the `OffchainVotedBadge` use colour-coded pills (green/red) like the on-chain badge for basic "For/Against/Abstain" proposals, or is the neutral style acceptable for all proposal types?
2. For multi-choice proposals, the local vote label shows all selected choices joined by comma. Is this the right truncation/display approach, or should it be limited?
3. After the page reload is removed, should we add an Apollo `refetchQueries` call in the background so the votes table also updates without requiring a manual reload?

body:
ix(auth): refresh when session expires and access_token falls back to id_token
Root cause of the Paxton 401 after ~15 minutes:

Express session expires after SESSION_EXPIRY (default 15 min)
openIdJwtStrategy falls back to using the id_token (Bearer token) as
federatedTokens.access_token when session.openidTokens is absent
id_token is still valid (~60-90 min), so isAccessTokenExpiredOrExpiringSoon
returned false and the middleware skipped the refresh
id_token is then forwarded to Paxton via {{LIBRECHAT_OPENID_ACCESS_TOKEN}}
placeholder -> Paxton returns 401 (wrong audience/token type)
Fix: check req.session.openidTokens.accessToken (the real OIDC access_token)
instead of req.user.federatedTokens.access_token (which may be the id_token
after session expiry). Refresh whenever the session access_token is absent
(session expired) OR expiring soon. OIDC refresh_token persists in a long-
lived httpOnly cookie so refresh is still possible after session expiry.

- UI behaviors include preventing adding tasks to past dates, duplicate-name handling with suggested postfix, inline editing on double-click, drag/drop to change completion state, and calendar day selection that filters tasks by entry date.

body:
## Discovery from this round
The two failures showed something important — **ABC's `request.requestBody` echo only includes fields ABC actually parsed**. From your test:

| We sent | ABC echoed |
|---|---|
| eventTypeId | ✅ |
| employeeId | ✅ |
| memberId | ✅ |
| allowUnfunded | ✅ |
| eventTimestamp | ❌ stripped |
| duration | ❌ stripped |
| eventTrainingLevelId | ❌ stripped |

So `eventTrainingLevelId`, `eventTimestamp`, and `duration` have been **silently ignored** the entire time. Wrong field names. We've been chasing the right shape with no signal.

## Two changes

### 1. Nested level shape (+ fallbacks)
ABC's GET returns `eventTrainingLevel: { levelId, levelName }`. POST is probably symmetric. So now the body sends:
\`\`\`json
{
  "eventTrainingLevel":   { "levelId": "..." },
  "eventTrainingLevelId": "...",
  "trainingLevelId":      "..."
}
\`\`\`
Whichever ABC actually parses will show up in the next echo. That tells us the right field name in one round.

### 2. Raw-sample debug
Real event data > guessing.
- New backend: `GET /abc-scheduler/event-types/:eventTypeId/raw-sample?club_number=` returns the full raw JSON of the most recent cached event for that event type.
- New **"Show ABC raw sample"** link next to the Training level field. Click → see the full event payload inline. Copy `eventTrainingLevel.levelId` from there into the manual input.

No more typing `"0"` or `"xzx...001"` — find a real ID from a real event.

## Next test plan
1. Merge + redeploy (both wcs-auth-api and portal static)
2. Open "+ Book event" → pick event type `aeeccf15186f4cfd8bc2f6e26c813ffd`
3. Click **"Show ABC raw sample"** → expand the JSON → find `eventTrainingLevel.levelId`
4. Paste that real ID into the manual training-level input
5. Submit
6. **Compare what we sent vs ABC's echo** in the debug block:
   - If ABC echoes `eventTrainingLevel: { levelId: ... }` → nested shape wins
   - If ABC echoes `eventTrainingLevelId: ...` → flat shape wins
   - If ABC echoes `trainingLevelId: ...` → alt naming wins
   - If none of them appear → all three shapes wrong, paste me the response and we try the next set

Once a shape is confirmed for level, we'll also need to fix the field names for `eventTimestamp` and `duration` (probably `eventTimestampLocal` and `durationMinutes` — but no point guessing until we know which dictionary ABC uses).

Replaces today's pattern of bouncing between ` /opportunity?lead= ` and ` /opportunity?deal= ` with one page that houses **everything about a person**: their conversations, their properties, their compliance state, their motivation signals.

- 4 header stats: Properties count, Outreach count, Status, Compliance state

**Three top-level tabs** — matches the tabs-discipline rule from the plan (max 2 levels of tabs, never nested):

| Tab | What |
|---|---|
| **Overview** | Next Action card · Recent Conversation (3 msgs) · Properties list · Highlights · Motivation Signals · Recent Activity · Quick Note composer |
| **Conversation** | Full SMS thread (left) · Compliance-gated composer with templates, merge tokens, char counter (right) · Quick disposition buttons |

If the lead is a TCPA litigator / on DNC / opted out, a full-width obsidian banner appears above the tab strip. Same gating as PR #6 — composer disabled, send blocked, the banner explains why.

Same client-side ` phone + owner_name ` grouping as the List Detail page. The current lead and all sibling properties owned by the same person appear in the Properties tab + Overview properties section.

### Demographics

No demographic fields render anywhere — ` age `, ` gender `, ` ethnic_group `, ` religion `, ` marital_status `, ` education_level `, ` occupation ` are imported but never displayed. Plan privacy guard honored.

author: davidcozens
body:
## Summary

- Replaces FreeRTOS-Plus-FAT (AWS Lab project, untagged, no consumer in SolidSyslog) with **FatFs (ChaN) R0.16** at \`/opt/fatfs\`, exposed via \`FATFS_PATH\` env var.
- FatFs is the de facto embedded filesystem (Zephyr, NuttX, MicroPython, STM32 HAL, ESP-IDF, Arduino SD ecosystem) — what integrators in the target user base already have. SolidSyslog [#270 (S08.05)](https://github.com/DavidCozens/solid-syslog/issues/270) lands shortly after this and targets FatFs as its embedded persistent-store backend.
- ChaN distributes FatFs as zip tarballs only (no upstream Git repo), so we pull from the long-running community mirror [\`abbrev/fatfs\`](https://github.com/abbrev/fatfs) which faithfully tags ChaN's official releases. Pinned to **R0.16** at SHA \`30ca13c62615df0d2e9104ab41256985b96590c1\`, SHA-gated like the other upstreams so a retagged mirror fails the build loudly.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI \`docker-publish\` workflow runs MIDDLE build clean — i.e. the new \`git clone --depth=1 --branch=R0.16 https://github.com/abbrev/fatfs.git /opt/fatfs\` resolves and SHA-gates pass.
- [ ] CI also rebuilds and republishes the TOP (cross) image FROMing the new MIDDLE SHA.
- [ ] On merge, capture the new \`sha-<short>\` tags published to GHCR — used by the follow-up SolidSyslog bump PR.

## Follow-up (separate PR in SolidSyslog repo)

Bump every reference to the old container SHA tag per \`docs/containers.md\` "Updating an image":

\`\`\`bash
grep -rln "cpputest-freertos:sha-10a14ae\|cpputest-freertos-cross:sha-10a14ae" .
\`\`\`

Title: \`chore: bump container image to <new-sha>\`. That bump is the prerequisite for SolidSyslog S08.05 slice 1.

## License compatibility

FatFs uses ChaN's permissive BSD-style license. The only obligation is preserving the copyright notice in \`ff.c\`, which is trivially satisfied — we vendor FatFs in the image and never modify \`ff.c\`. \`diskio.c\` is the integrator's port file by FatFs's own design and is expected to be replaced downstream.

author: matthewharwood
body:
## Summary

Comprehensive documentation initiative. 14 READMEs (1 root + 11 crate + 2 tool, 4 NEW) on a consistent template that GitHub renders natively. CLAUDE.md gains a section codifying the rules so future READMEs follow the same shape automatically.

## What changed

### New READMEs (4)

- \`crates/media/README.md\` — clock + audio + histogram + waveform geometry + capture + manifest.
- \`crates/dev-server/README.md\` — axum + WebSocket live-reload + Tailscale-ready remote dev.
- \`tools/doc-gates/README.md\` — four CI gates on one Rust binary.
- \`tools/mdbook-preprocessor-cross/README.md\` — \`{{shared}}\` / \`{{wisp-link}}\` mechanics.

### Existing READMEs — full rewrites (10)

Every crate README now follows the same 9-section template:

1. Title + tagline + blockquote summary
2. **What it does** — problem framing
3. **Where it fits** — one mermaid diagram with the shared class palette
4. **Quickstart** — ≤10 lines to something visible
5. **Hero output** — existing committed asset, no new images
6. **Public API at a glance** — top 5-10 items table
7. **Runbook** — Build+test / Run / Common tasks / Troubleshooting
8. **Deep dive** — book chapter / examples / sibling READMEs / CLAUDE.md
9. **License**

### Root README

- ASCII-art arch diagram → mermaid \`flowchart TD\` with consistent class palette (orange = wisp, green = media, indigo = UI, slate = shell).
- Curated \"What you'll see\" screenshot row.
- Status table updated through DOCS-11 and M-MEDIA.0..14.
- Stack table fixed (drop ffmpeg-next; Leptos 0.8; two-book layout; three-OS CI matrix).
- Workflow restructured around a \`sequenceDiagram\` showing the 11-step contract.
- New CI matrix table summarising the macOS-truth / Ubuntu-lavapipe / Windows-DX12 split.

### CLAUDE.md

New section \"README authoring — GitHub-readable, no preprocessing\":

- READMEs use GFM, NOT \`mdbook-preprocessor-cross\` tags.
- Canonical 9-section structure with class-palette mapping.
- GFM callouts (\`> [!NOTE]\` etc.) vs mdBook admonish — when to use which.
- DRY pattern via \`mdbook-cmdrun\` when README ↔ book chapter would share content.
- The five most-cited callout types + their use cases.

## Why

Three drivers:

1. **Per-crate discoverability at the GitHub level.** Click any crate dir on github.com → immediately understand what it does, how to run it, what it depends on, where the deep dive lives. Previously most crate READMEs were 50-line command lists.
2. **Architectural visibility.** Every crate's place in the dataflow is now one mermaid diagram, rendered natively by GitHub. No more reading the root README to figure out who depends on whom.
3. **Anti-rot.** Codifying the template + class palette + callout conventions in CLAUDE.md means the next contributor (human or Claude) follows the same shape automatically.

## Test plan

- [x] \`just gate\` green (10 stages including doc-gates).
- [x] Every hero image referenced in READMEs exists.
- [x] Mermaid blocks use the shared class palette consistently.
- [x] \`actionlint\` clean.
- [ ] Reviewer check: render every README on GitHub PR diff view, verify mermaid + callouts + images all render.

- **`AdminContext.jsx`**: capture `capabilities` from the `/api/admin/auth/me` response (was already returned by the backend, just not plumbed through). Expose `capabilities` + `hasCapability(cap)` from `useAdmin()`. `login()` + `setup()` trigger a refresh so capabilities populate after password flows.
- **`AdminStaffDetail.jsx`**: AccessTab's `canInvite` prop now reads `hasCapability('staff.invite')` instead of `hasRole('manager')`. Backend `POST /:id/invite` already enforces this capability — the frontend change just stops showing the button to users who'd get 403'd anyway.

### Remote D1 mutation (operator-authorized)

```sql
DELETE FROM role_preset_capabilities
WHERE capability_key = 'staff.invite'
  AND role_preset_key = 'booking_coordinator';
-- 1 row removed
```

After the mutation, `staff.invite` is bound to: **owner**, **event_director** — exactly the operator's intended allow-list, minus HR (see below).

## HR — follow-up

There's no `hr_coordinator` role_preset yet (the role `role_hr_coordinator` exists in the role catalog, but no matching preset exists in `role_presets`). When an HR person is onboarded, the operator (or a small follow-up PR) creates the preset + binds the appropriate capabilities including `staff.invite`. Any user assigned to the preset via `users.role_preset_key='hr_coordinator'` then inherits invite access automatically. ~2 SQL statements.

## Verification

- Dev-server browser: Paul has 96 capabilities (owner preset) including `staff.invite` → invite button visible + enabled, modal works as before.
- After deploy on a hypothetical user with only the `booking_coordinator` preset, the button would be hidden (and even if it weren't, the backend would 403).

All 2056 tests pass. Lint 0 errors. Build clean.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Merge + deploy
- [ ] Paul: invite button still visible on Access tab → modal works as before
- [ ] If you create a test user on `booking_coordinator` preset: invite button hidden on their Access tab; if they hit the API directly they get 403

author: chriscrosstalk
body:
## What

`rewriteQueryWithContext` in `admin/app/controllers/ollama_controller.ts` short-circuits the conversation-aware query rewriter when `userMessages.length <= 2`. That bound skips not just the first turn (where there's nothing to rewrite) but also the **first follow-up** (where the rewriter is most needed). Result: any chat that has had exactly one prior exchange sends RAG the raw latest message as the query, embeddings match nothing relevant (the prior turn's entities are gone), no RAG system message is injected, and the assistant answers the follow-up as if it were a brand-new, context-less question.

This PR changes the threshold to `< 2` so the rewriter runs from the first follow-up onward, matching the original behavior prior to commit `96e5027` (2026-03-11).

## Why

User scenario reproduced on NOMAD3 running v1.32.0-rc.3 with `mistral-nemo:12b`:

| Turn | Message |
|---|---|
| 1 (user) | "my 30lb terrier just ate 3 Hershey's bars about 30 minutes ago - we are snowed in and can't get to the vet…" |
| 1 (assistant) | Correctly retrieves chocolate-poisoning context, answers with theobromine math, induce-vomiting guidance, etc. |
| 2 (user) | "great - they threw up 2 of the bars it looks like" |
| 2 (assistant, pre-patch) | "Relevant Context: None. Since there is no relevant context provided regarding throwing up bars for s'more peanut butter bars or related recipes…" → drifts into recipe troubleshooting |

The pronoun "the bars" without rewriting embeds to recipe content far more strongly than to canine chocolate toxicity. Once the rewriter is skipped, RAG returns nothing above the 0.3 similarity threshold and the model loses the thread.

## How

```diff
-      // Skip rewriting for short conversations. Rewriting adds latency with
-      // little RAG benefit until there is enough context to matter.
+      // Skip rewriting on the very first turn — with only one user message
+      // there is no prior context to fold in, so the rewrite would just echo
+      // the message back at the cost of an extra LLM round-trip. From the
+      // first follow-up onward we need the rewrite so the RAG query carries
+      // entities and topics from earlier turns ("the bars" → "Hershey's bars
+      // chocolate poisoning dog"); without it, embeddings match nothing and
+      // the assistant loses the thread.
       const userMessages = recentMessages.filter(msg => msg.role === 'user')
-      if (userMessages.length <= 2) {
+      if (userMessages.length < 2) {
         return lastUserMessage?.content || null
       }
```

The original perf-motivation comment isn't wrong — it's just that rewriting on turn 2 IS worthwhile, and the latency cost (one extra small-model round-trip) is the price of correct context carry. Turn 1 with only one user message still short-circuits, so there's no added latency on first message.

## Verification

Hot-patched the compiled controller into the NOMAD3 admin container and replayed the dog-chocolate scenario via `POST /api/ollama/chat` with the same three-message conversation. Pre-patch behavior matches the reporter's screenshot (pivots to recipes). Post-patch:

> "Based on the provided knowledge base contexts, none directly relate to chocolate poisoning in dogs. However… **Because my dog threw up 2 out of the 3 consumed chocolate bars**, it's likely that we caught symptoms early and minimized much worse effects. However, **I would strongly recommend contacting my vet right away**…"

The "3 chocolate bars" detail is the smoking gun — that fact appears only in turn 1, which the unpatched build was effectively dropping. Post-patch the model carries it forward correctly.

## Notes

- One-line code change with expanded comment explaining intent for future readers.
- Targeted at `rc` since v1.32.0-rc.3 just dropped and this regression has been live since v1.31.x (commit landed 2026-03-11). Worth getting into rc.4 if we're cutting one before GA.
- A secondary, pre-existing issue surfaced during testing on this fix: RAG can over-match on semantic-similar-but-clinically-wrong content (a radiation-sickness chunk scored 74.3% relevance on a warfarin-headache follow-up), and small models like `mistral-nemo:12b` anchor on the bad chunk instead of dismissing it per `rag_context` rule 4. That's a separate retrieval-tuning conversation (raise 0.3 threshold? strengthen "ignore irrelevant" instruction?) and out of scope here.

author: saddlepaddle
body:
## Summary

`superset auth login` over-eagerly shelled out to `xdg-open` on any TTY where `CI` / `SSH_CONNECTION` / `SSH_TTY` were unset. In real-world headless boxes that gap meant:

- **`SSH_CLIENT` was ignored.** openssh sets `SSH_CLIENT` but skips `SSH_CONNECTION` under certain PAM stacks / `UseDNS no` configs. A user SSH'd into an EC2 instance hit the auto-open path and ended up with a mangled URL pasted into their local Chrome — which then failed with `[query.response_type] Invalid input: expected "code"` against better-auth's Zod schema.
- **Linux + no DISPLAY / WAYLAND_DISPLAY → `xdg-open` is a no-op.** Same outcome: the URL gets thrown at the terminal in whatever shape the launcher prints it.
- **No `--no-browser` escape hatch** for users who want a clean paste flow even in a "headed" terminal.

## What changed

- Extracted browser-eligibility into `detectHeadlessReason(env)` — pure, returns a reason string or `null`. New checks: `SSH_CLIENT`, container env (`CONTAINER=docker`, `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST`), Superset remote workspaces (`SUPERSET_REMOTE_WORKSPACE`), and Linux/BSD without `DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`. macOS and Windows still skip the display check (OS-level URL handlers).
- Added `--no-browser` flag to `superset auth login`.
- LoginUI swaps the prompt from `Browser didn't open?` to `Open this URL on a machine with a browser to sign in` when we already know the browser was never going to open.
- Added regression-guard tests on `buildAuthorizeUrl` confirming `response_type=code` is always set (the value the server's better-auth Zod schema requires).

## Why this fixes the SSH paste error too

Curl'ing the live URL builds verifies the API accepts the params as the CLI generates them. The validation error in the Slack thread was the symptom of a URL that got copy-paste-mangled out of an SSH terminal — auto-open chose `xdg-open` (which can't reach a browser on a remote box), the URL was dumped onto the terminal in whatever encoding the launcher emitted, and the user pasted a clipped copy into their local Chrome. Skipping auto-open on SSH means the URL is printed cleanly via clack/Ink (which we control), so the paste works.

Slack thread: user (Daniel) SSH'd into `ec2-user@ip-172-31-24-214`, ran `superset auth login`.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun --filter=@superset/cli test` — 22 new tests pass
- [x] `bun --filter=@superset/cli typecheck` clean
- [x] `bun run lint` clean
- [ ] Manual: `ssh` into a Linux box, run `superset auth login` from a fresh build, confirm browser is not launched and the URL is printed
- [ ] Manual: `superset auth login --no-browser` on macOS prints URL without opening Safari
- [ ] Manual: vanilla `superset auth login` on macOS still opens the browser

author: pcameron80
body:
## Summary

Cuts deploy time for code-only changes from ~6 min back to under 1 min.

The April 30 egress reduction added a prebuild step (\`scripts/build-match-data.ts\`) that pre-computes ~23,000 cross-brand match JSON files to \`public/match-data/\`. Without the prebuild, color pages hit Supabase on every render (~300 MB egress per million renders). With it, deploys went from ~45s to ~6m — and the prebuild runs on **every** deploy, even when the underlying data hasn't changed.

This PR adds a cache shortcut. Vercel preserves \`.next/cache/\` between deploys, so we persist the generated JSON files there plus a marker containing a content hash.

## How it works

\`\`\`
prebuild start
  ├─ get current hash = count(cross_brand_matches) | count(colors)   (~200ms)
  ├─ marker in .next/cache exists?
  │    └─ yes → hash matches?
  │         └─ yes → copy .next/cache/match-data/* to public/match-data/  ← FAST PATH
  │              exit (skip 5min regeneration)
  └─ no or hash mismatch → full regeneration (existing path)
       └─ at the end, copy public/match-data/* to .next/cache/match-data/
          + write marker → cached for next build
\`\`\`

## Hash choice

Row counts on both tables (\`cross_brand_matches\`, \`colors\`). Both are head-count queries so they're cheap (no row scan). Sufficient because:
- \`cross_brand_matches\` is append-only — it's rewritten in bulk by \`scripts/compute-matches.ts\` and never edited in place
- \`colors\` only changes when \`scripts/import-*.ts\` runs

Edge case: rows edited in place without count changes would produce a stale cache. Doesn't happen in normal operation. Fix is to run \`rm -rf .next/cache\` and redeploy.

## Test plan

- [ ] First preview deploy builds normally (~6 min) — cache miss path
- [ ] Second preview deploy on the same branch with no data change — should complete in under 1 min (cache hit path)
- [ ] Build log shows \"Cache hit\" message and file copy count
- [ ] Color detail pages still serve correct match data (verify a few with curl)
- [ ] After merge, watch first 2-3 production deploys to confirm short-circuit is firing

## Notes

- Independent of PR #31 (color-page generateStaticParams). Can ship either order.
- Conservative implementation — if the cache mechanism breaks for any reason, falls back to the full regeneration path. Worst case is the current behavior.

author: donovan-yohan
body:
## Summary

Design-only spike for the three security primitives that unblock the #427 security backbone epic. New doc at `docs/spikes/422-capability-bits-rotation-confirmation.md`. No code changes.

## MVP recommendations

- **Capability bits live hub-side** in an ACL store keyed by an opaque `aclRef`. The credential carries only the ref + a version counter; bits never travel to the node. Policy changes are atomic and don't require re-pairing. Default-grant migration for existing credentials (no force re-pair).
- **Credential rotation** is a hub-initiated `STABLE → ISSUING → DELIVERED → PROVED` state machine delivered over the existing `/hub/node-link` reverse channel via a new `control.rotate-credential` envelope. Node writes the new credential file atomically (temp+rename), reconnects with the new token, hub revokes the old token only after the new link is proven. Default 30-day rotation, configurable, manual + scheduled + policy-driven triggers.
- **Two-token confirmation** uses the **hub UI on a second authenticated browser session** as the MVP channel — no new dependencies, no push provider, no TOTP setup. Token is a `confirm_*` opaque value with `{scope, ttl: 90s, single-use, hmac-signed}` shape. The channel is pluggable so WebAuthn / push-to-phone can layer in later.
- Rotation does **not** invalidate existing sessions on routine hygiene rotates; ACL-bit removal does re-validate open sessions (#426).
- ADR-015 and ADR-016 compliance verified: bits are core, verb-to-bit translation is feature-layer; confirmation tokens are hub-issued and hub-redeemed, never routed through peer nodes.

## Follow-up tickets named in the spike (to be filed as sub-issues of #427)

1. Capability-bit ACL store + schema
2. `RelayNodeCredential` aclRef + aclVersion fields
3. Hub policy evaluator + session gate
4. Confirmation challenge + token registry
5. Confirmation events on `/ws/events`
6. Frontend confirmation prompt component
7. Credential rotation state machine
8. Scheduled rotation + per-node policy
9. `relay-ide node rotate-credential` (hub-side CLI)
10. Re-validate open sessions on ACL change
11. `docs/federated-relay.md` Security Model update

## Test plan

- [ ] Reviewer reads the spike and confirms the MVP choices in §2 (hub-side ACL), §3 (rotation over reverse link), §4 (hub-UI-on-second-device confirmation) are acceptable.
- [ ] Reviewer agrees with the verb-to-bit table in §2.3.
- [ ] Reviewer confirms the threat list in §5 is complete and honest about what is NOT mitigated.
- [ ] Reviewer agrees the 11 follow-up tickets are appropriately scoped for belayer runs.
- [ ] After merge: file tickets 1–11 as sub-issues of #427 (use `/ticket`).

Closes #422.

author: octagent
body:
## What this is

First PR in a stacked series that ports the **Lossless Context Management** algorithm into Pawrrtal.  Inspired by Martian-Engineering's TypeScript OpenClaw plugin; rebuilt natively in Python + Postgres because their plugin shell can't run inside our FastAPI stack.

See `docs/design/lcm.md` for the full plan and `.beans/lcm-followups.md` for the running deferred-work list.

## Stack roadmap

1. ✅ **schema + models** — *this PR*
2. ⏭ ingest + assembly (fresh tail only)
3. ⏭ leaf compaction
4. ⏭ `lcm_grep` tool
5. ⏭ `lcm_describe` tool
6. ⏭ `lcm_expand_query`
7. ⏭ condensation pass

Each is a small tracer-bullet PR.  Deferred items per step go into `.beans/lcm-followups.md`.

## What lands here (schema only)

### Three new ORM classes in `backend/app/models.py`

- **`LCMSummary`** — a summary node.  `depth=0` is a leaf (summarises raw messages); `depth>=1` is a condensed parent.  Carries `summary_kind` (`normal` / `aggressive` / `fallback`) for the three-level escalation we'll implement in PR #3.
- **`LCMSummarySource`** — link table from a summary to its source items.  String discriminator (`source_kind=message|summary`) so one parent can mix raw messages and child summaries during condensation.
- **`LCMContextItem`** — the ordered 'replacement list' walked per turn.  Each row points at either a `ChatMessage` or an `LCMSummary`.  Compaction rewrites this list in place by replacing a contiguous range of message rows with a summary row, then renumbering ordinals densely.

### Alembic migration `012_add_lcm_tables`

Creates the three tables + indices + the unique `(conversation_id, ordinal)` constraint on `lcm_context_items` so compaction's renumber stays safe.

### Settings (default-off)

```env
LCM_ENABLED=false                    # master switch
LCM_FRESH_TAIL_COUNT=64              # recent messages always kept verbatim
LCM_LEAF_CHUNK_TOKENS=20000          # source-token ceiling per leaf summary
LCM_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD=0.75           # fraction of window that triggers compaction
LCM_INCREMENTAL_MAX_DEPTH=1          # condensation passes per compaction (-1 = unlimited)
LCM_SUMMARY_MODEL=                   # override; falls back to conversation model
```

Defaults match the upstream plugin's choices.

### Docs

- `docs/design/lcm.md` — problem, approach, schema, config, roadmap, divergence from upstream
- `.beans/lcm-followups.md` — deferred-work running list

## What's deliberately NOT in this PR

- Any code that reads or writes the new tables (PR #2)
- Compaction logic (PR #3)
- Agent tools: `lcm_grep`, `lcm_describe`, `lcm_expand_query` (PRs #4-6)
- Condensation pass (PR #7)
- `/lcm` operational commands (deferred indefinitely)

Because `LCM_ENABLED` defaults to `false`, this PR **cannot** change runtime behaviour for any existing deployment.  It's a pure data-model addition.

## Tests (5 new)

`backend/tests/test_lcm_schema.py`:
- Summary insert round-trips with all fields preserved.
- `lcm_summary_sources` accepts a mix of `message` + `summary` discriminators in a single parent (the condensation use case).
- `(conversation_id, ordinal)` unique constraint actually fires on conflict.
- Every LCM FK declares `ON DELETE CASCADE` (runtime cascade is enforced by Postgres in prod — SQLite tests can't exercise it without enabling `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, which would scope-creep this PR.  Metadata pin is enough to catch a future regression.)
- LCM settings have safe off-by-default values.

Full backend suite: **374 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed** (was 369; +5 new).

## Why a Python port instead of vendoring their code

The upstream plugin is built around OpenClaw's `ContextEngine` plugin lifecycle (bootstrap / ingest / assemble / afterTurn / compact) — none of which exists in our FastAPI codebase.  Stitching a Node.js sidecar in for every chat turn would add deploy complexity for one feature.  Porting the algorithm to Python is ~800-1200 LOC across the stack vs.~ ~5k LOC of plugin shell coupled with OpenClaw's gateway runtime.

We kept their core architectural choices (DAG, fresh-tail protection, three-level escalation, the tool surface) and adapted the storage (SQLite → Postgres) and integration point (plugin lifecycle → FastAPI route + agent_tools).

## Summary
- Introduces a `UserService` class in the service layer that encapsulates all CRUD and lifecycle operations for `UserProfile` records
- Adds Pydantic schemas (`UserCreateSchema`, `UserUpdateSchema`, `UserReponseSchema`) to validate and serialize user data at the service boundary
- Wires up pytest infrastructure and a comprehensive test suite covering the full user lifecycle

## Changes
- `backend/db/services/user_profile_service.py` — New `UserService` class with methods: `create_user_profile`, `get_user_profile_by_id`, `update_user_profile`, `deactivate_user`, and `reactivate_user`. Includes custom `InactiveUserError` raised when a mutation targets an inactive profile.
- `backend/schemas/users.py` — Pydantic schemas for create, update, and response shapes; `UserReponseSchema` uses `from_attributes=True` for ORM compatibility.
- `backend/tests/services/test_user_profile_service.py` — 290-line test suite covering creation, retrieval (`raise_err` variants), update validation, deactivation, and reactivation.
- `backend/pyproject.toml` / `backend/uv.lock` — Project and lockfile initialized for the backend Python package.

## Related Issues
<!-- If this addresses an open issue, replace N below -->
<!-- closes #N -->

## Testing
- [x] Run `pytest backend/tests/services/test_user_profile_service.py` and confirm all tests pass
- [x] Verify `deactivate_user` and `reactivate_user` are idempotent (no error on repeated calls)
- [x] Confirm `update_user_profile` raises `InactiveUserError` for deactivated users
- [x] Confirm `get_user_profile_by_id(raise_err=False)` returns `None` for missing IDs instead of raising

## Notes for Reviewer
- `active` is intentionally excluded from `UserUpdateSchema` and `update_user_profile`. Activation state is managed exclusively through `deactivate_user` / `reactivate_user`, and inactive users are explicitly blocked from profile updates via `InactiveUserError`. This keeps the two concerns separate and prevents accidental reactivation through a generic update call.
- `InactiveUserError` is intentionally separate from SQLAlchemy's `NoResultFound` — callers need to distinguish "user doesn't exist" from "user exists but is inactive."
- `update_user_profile` validates kwargs against `UserUpdateSchema` before touching the DB, so unknown fields are rejected at the schema level.

## Summary

- Adds a design spec treating durable DPF governance as a first-class `principle` wiki kind, with tiered taxonomy (commandment / core / contextual), schema extension on `WikiPage`, an advisory `principle_decide` MCP tool with explicit signed dimension vectors, kernel-markdown-driven public docs, and a 7-batch migration plan.
- Distills the current scatter — ~16 principle-shaped rules in `AGENTS.md`, the 8 existing AI coworker principles in this branch, ~42 candidate memory entries, and 3+ buried in EP-WIKI-001 — into a single substrate retrievable by in-platform coworkers and external coding agents through passive recall and `wiki_query`.
- Decision math is advisory-only: every recommendation comes with a per-principle contribution ledger, structured-vs-semantic alignment flags, tie warnings, and commandment-conflict surfacing. TAK/HITL stays authoritative.

## Background

Founder articulated a principle-based governance philosophy with vector-matrix decision aggregation as "the purist approach" for multi-parameter option comparison. The formulation aligns with established MCDM (AHP, TOPSIS, weighted-sum) and rides EP-WIKI-001's existing Qdrant + lint + retrieval substrate rather than introducing parallel infrastructure.

## Chief-architect review applied

💡 **What:** Added `useMemo` to the `bestOrm` (best One-Rep Max) derived state calculation in the `ExerciseGroup` component within `WorkoutActive.js`. Extracted the logic from an inline Immediately Invoked Function Expression (IIFE) in the JSX render block. Also fixed a lingering lint warning in `MetricsLog.js`.
🎯 **Why:** The `WorkoutActive` page contains an active timer interval that updates the `elapsed` state every second. This causes a full re-render of the parent and its children on every tick. Previously, the `bestOrm` was being recalculated from the `pbs` array inline during every single render cycle, creating unnecessary CPU work and potentially slowing down the UI over time.
📊 **Impact:** Prevents redundant `Array.prototype.reduce` execution every second during active workouts. Reduces unnecessary computations by 100% per unchanged PB array state during the duration of the workout, freeing up the main thread and improving rendering stability on low-end devices.
🔬 **Measurement:** Verify by running the application, opening an active workout containing multiple sets with PBs, and observing that the 1RM estimate remains correctly rendered while ensuring (via React Profiler) the reduction isn't executed on every timer tick. Build and test validation has also been passed (`npm run build`, `npm run test --passWithNoTests`).

author: stormer78
body:
## Summary

Phase 3 PR 3/5. Lands the trust-registry reconciler's policy-aware behaviour:

- **M3.5** — `MembershipSyncer` consults `registry.rego.publish_on_join` at dispatch time. PublishMember jobs short-circuit to `Complete` (no HTTP call) when the active policy returns `false`.
- **M3.6** — `min_disposition` floor clamps non-RTBF removals up to the operator's preservation floor. Member-initiated `Purge` (actor == target) bypasses the clamp per spec §8.2 and emits `RegistryRecordPolicyOverride` audit envelopes. No override envelope when the clamp wouldn't have fired — keeps the audit log focused on actionable signals.
- **M3.7** — RTBF-flagged jobs are parked with `next_attempt_at = now + rtbf_batch_window_hours` (default 24h) so the registry record's disappearance can't be timed-aligned with the override event. Configurable via `registry.rtbf_batch_window_hours`; `0` disables batching (test convenience).
- **M3.8** — `GET /v1/health/diagnostics` (AdminAuth) surfaces queue_depth, rtbf_batched_count, failed_count, oldest_pending_age_seconds (excludes future-dated RTBF rows), plus registry_status / last_success / last_failure / last_error from `RegistryHealth`. Trust Task `health/diagnostics/1.0` ships with spec.md + schema.json + index entry.

### Key design notes

- **Severity is preservation-based.** `historical > tombstone > purge` — the operator's floor is the minimum record retention they'll accept, not the privacy strength. Matches the default `registry.rego` shipping `min_disposition := "purge"` (no clamp) and makes the RTBF override semantically meaningful when operators raise the floor.
- **Policy resolution happens at the walker / dispatch boundary.** A freshly-uploaded policy takes effect on the next tick without bouncing the daemon — no warm-up, no cache invalidation surface.
- **Override audit envelope emission is fire-and-forget after the SyncJob is durably enqueued.** A daemon crash between enqueue and audit-emit re-walks the same `MemberRemoved` envelope on next boot (cursor hasn't advanced past it yet) and re-emits. Duplicate override envelope is a less-bad failure mode than a silent override.
- **`RegistryConfig` gets an explicit `Default` impl** so the derived zeros don't silently disable batching / the periodic probe in code paths that hit the default.

## Test plan

- [x] 54 registry unit tests pass (`registry::policy`, `registry::tail`, `registry::syncer`, `registry::upstream`, `registry::storage`, `registry::model`)
- [x] 4 diagnostics integration tests pass (empty queue, populated queue with pending+RTBF+failed, role gating, Trust-Task gating)
- [x] Full `cargo test --package vtc-service` green (262 lib + every integration suite)
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --package vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] DCO sign-off on commit

## Out of scope

- M3.9 (foreign-credential verifier) — next PR
- M3.10 (cross-community session-mint hardening) — next PR
- DIDComm transport for `UpstreamRegistryClient::{publish_member,delete_member}` — deferred to M3.10 follow-up
