author: etacassiopeia
body:
## Summary

The `structuredLogging.elapsed`, `metricsDetailed.after`, and `metricsDetailed.error` hooks read the recorded start time from `HookData` to compute evaluation duration. The existing code used `hookData.get(key).getOrElse(end)` which allocates an `Option` on every flag evaluation — a hot path.

Adds `HookData.getOrNull(key): Any` (internal, `private[openfeature]`) that returns the raw value or `null`, and updates the three duration call sites to pattern-match on `null`. As a side benefit, when no start time was recorded (defensive case), the read of the end-time clock is skipped entirely and `Duration.Zero` is returned.

`Clock.nanoTime` is preserved (consistent with both `before` and tests), so `TestClock` interactions remain correct.

## Changes

- `Hook.scala`: add `HookData.getOrNull` (internal API)
- `Hook.scala`: rewrite `structuredLogging.elapsed`, `metricsDetailed.after`, `metricsDetailed.error` to use null-first pattern match

@EtaCassiopeia 

## Credit

Spotted in #110 by @guizmaii. The original PR also switched `Clock.nanoTime` → `System.nanoTime`; this PR keeps `Clock.nanoTime` for testability.

author: alanhuang99
body:
Stacked on #8 (Milestone A). Merge after that one.

## Summary

- **B1 + B5**: `PayloadReceiverHandler` writes off the event loop. Serial `DispatchQueue` chained on completion futures so file writes stay ordered. Per-chunk `Array(readableBytesView)` replaced with one sized `Data` copy from `withUnsafeReadableBytes`. Multi-GB receives no longer starve the control-plane channel sharing the loop.
- **B2**: `PluginRegistry` caches `allIncomingCapabilities` / `allOutgoingCapabilities`. Identity broadcasts (every 5 s) no longer rebuild the Set and re-sort. Cache invalidated on `register` and on `Settings.setPluginEnabled`.
- **B3**: UDP broadcast uses a long-lived socket opened in `start()` / closed in `stop()` instead of socket-create-close per tick.
- **B4**: `firstLF` tracks how far it has scanned across `channelRead` calls. Small chunked reads on long pre-newline payloads no longer re-walk the prefix every read.
- **B6**: `-strict-concurrency=complete` enabled on both targets. One real warning fixed (`LanLinkProvider`'s UDP `newConnectionHandler` was capturing weak self inside a Sendable nested closure).

## Deviations from brief

- **B1 backpressure**: shipped as queue-chained writes only. NIO's autoread still drives reads as fast as the network delivers; if the disk is genuinely slower than the network the writeQueue's task list can grow. Real backpressure (`NIOAsyncChannel` or autoread suspend) is a follow-up — see WORK_LOG.md.

## Test plan

- [x] `swift build` — clean with strict concurrency.
- [x] `swift test` — 8 / 8.
- [ ] Manual: send a 200 MB file while a ping / clipboard exchange is in flight; control-plane should stay snappy.

body:
## Summary
- Extend `SYS_SYS_PIPELINE2` to a 4-pointer ABI (`SI=left_path`, `DI=right_path`, `DX=left_args`, `CX=right_args`) so pipeline children can receive argv the same way `exec()`'d programs do.
- Kernel `.stage_pipeline_child_args` helper stages each child's args bytes into the shell's `BUFFER` slot and writes `EXEC_ARG = BUFFER` immediately before the per-child `.populate_handoff_from_shell` call.  The existing handoff-frame copy carries both into the child's user_data frame at matching offsets, so `FUNCTION_PARSE_ARGV` resolves argv through the child's PD with no extra plumbing.
- Shell splits each side at the first unquoted space; passes the args tail (or `NULL`) via the new pipeline2 builtin.  Two new BSS arrays (`pipe_left_args` / `pipe_right_args`) hold the per-child argv strings.
- Folds `pipe_spam_ignore.c` into `pipe_spam.c` (`pipe_spam ignore` installs SIG_IGN, plain `pipe_spam` keeps SIG_DFL) and updates `test_sigpipe.py` accordingly.
- Adds `tests/test_pipeline_args.py` covering `pipe_producer bulk | pipe_consumer` (16384-byte ring traversal) and `pipe_producer early | pipe_consumer` (1 byte + exit-7 status).

## Description

When loading the URDF for a `RobotModel`, `rviz` does not use the `material` defined in the URDF. `AssimpLoader` appears to set a default material (grey-ish, diffuse lighting, not named `BaseWhite...`). `RobotLink::assignMaterialsToEntities()` currently uses this default material instead `default_material_` which comes from the URDF via `getMaterialForLink()`.

author: aristocles
body:
# What changed

The HAE discovery card's \"N more metrics received but not supported
yet\" footer gains a **\"Dismiss all\"** button next to the expand
chevron. Clicking it fans out to the existing per-metric dismiss
endpoint in parallel, wiping every undismissed unsupported metric in
one click. Per-row Dismiss buttons removed as part of the
simplification.

Also pins the E2E sandbox server's TZ to the host's timezone so
writeable-card date checks don't drift from the browser's local
date. Latent bug surfaced while wiring up the mood-daily-prompt
spec.

Fixes #218.

# Why

Operator's 2026-05-12 QA feedback:

> There should be a button for 'dismiss all'. In fact, there doesn't
> need to be a dismiss for each of them. Just the dismiss all.

On a configured instance, 15+ unsupported metrics can sit in the
footer. Dismissing one-by-one is painful and not worth the UX
budget — the operator's already decided they don't want any of
these. Un-hide from Settings remains the rescue hatch for anyone
who changes their mind.

# How

**\`eh-hae-discovery-card.js\`**:

- New \`_dismissAllUnsupported()\` method mirrors the existing
  \`_dismissCategory()\` pattern: collect the current metric keys,
  fan out \`POST /dismiss\` calls in parallel, update local state.
- \`_renderUnsupportedFooter()\` gains a two-button header row (flex
  layout) with the toggle on the left and \"Dismiss all\" on the
  right.
- Per-row Dismiss buttons removed. Expanded list is now purely
  informational — operator sees what's in there but can't
  selectively dismiss.

**Sandbox seed** extends \`discovered.json\` from one unsupported
metric to three so the \"dismiss all\" spec asserts on a meaningful
fan-out.

**TZ fix in \`global-setup.js\`**: the sandbox server's \`ENV.TZ\`
defaulted to UTC but the host / browser use local TZ. On a host
where local date is a day ahead of UTC (AEST etc.), rows seeded
at local-today get flagged as \"future-dated\" by the server's
allowance check. Surfaced in the mood-daily-prompt spec as a 403
on the restore-state call. Now \`global-setup\` passes
\`TZ: Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone\` into
\`spawnServer\` so all three clocks agree.

# Testing

New E2E spec \`tests-e2e/discovery-dismiss-all-unsupported.spec.js\`:

1. Seeds \`discovered.json\` with three unsupported metrics.
2. Loads Today view.
3. Asserts the footer is visible (renders \"N metrics received
   but not supported yet\").
4. Clicks the Dismiss-all button (which must be visible without
   expanding).
5. Asserts the footer text is gone (footer suppressed when
   unsupportedCount drops to zero).
6. Reads \`/api/health-auto-export/discoveries\` and asserts all
   three seeded metric keys land in the \`dismissed\` list.

Verified fails against main. Passes with the implementation.

- [x] \`npm test\` — 827/828 pass locally (pre-existing Windows
      \`no-personal-refs\` flake; CI green)
- [x] \`npm run test:e2e\` — 22/22 pass (up from 21 with the new
      spec)
- [x] Fail-on-main verified for the new spec
- [x] TZ fix doesn't change any existing spec's behaviour; they
      all still pass

# Checklist

- [x] Commit messages follow conventions
- [x] \`CHANGELOG.md\` updated
- [x] Inline comment on the new header flex layout explains the
      #218 design intent
- [x] No personal identifiers or hardcoded paths introduced
- [x] No secrets or high-entropy tokens committed

# Follow-up

Remaining from the 2026-05-12 QA triage:

- #185 — Schedule prompt modal reminder-flow redesign (awaiting
  UX sign-off)
- #216 — Weight/BP \`type:number\` (likely no-action per #189's
  measuring vs counting rule of thumb)
- #217 — \`writeable.prefillFromLatest\` enhancement
- #195 — Manifest-driven starter prompts (biggest remaining item)

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

```bash
      --profile string       Apply values from a saved profile (see 'pushover-pp-cli profile list')
      --quiet                Bare output, one value per line
      --rate-limit float     Max requests per second (0 to disable)
      --select string        Comma-separated fields to include in output (e.g. --select id,name,status)
      --timeout duration     Request timeout (default 30s)
  -v, --version              version for pushover-pp-cli
      --yes                  Skip confirmation prompts (for agents and scripts)

Use "pushover-pp-cli [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

### Novel Commands

| Command | Name | Description |
|---------|------|-------------|
| `notify` | Agent send wrapper | Send a notification from an argument or stdin with env/config defaults, named priorities, and emergency validation. |
| `emergency watch` | Emergency lifecycle | Send or monitor an emergency notification receipt, polling acknowledgement status and supporting cancellation. |
| `quota` | Quota cockpit | Show monthly send limit, remaining sends, and reset time from the app limits endpoint. |
| `history` | Local notification ledger | Search and export a local redacted ledger of notifications sent by this CLI and receipt outcomes. |
| `inbox sync` | Inbox sync/search | Download Open Client messages into local SQLite before optional server-side delete-through. |

### What This CLI Does

`pushover-pp-cli` wraps Pushover's full API surface: messages, receipts, glances, sounds, devices, subscriptions, licenses, the Open Client inbox, and the Teams admin API. Every endpoint is exposed as a Cobra subcommand and an MCP tool (26 typed tools). Beyond mirroring the API, it adds:

- **Agent-safe send wrapper** (`notify`) — read message from positional arg or stdin, set device/priority/sound/url defaults from env or config, validate emergency-priority `retry`/`expire` before sending so the call doesn't 400 server-side.
- **Emergency receipt lifecycle** (`emergency watch`) — poll the receipt API for an acked-by-user status with backoff and a cancellation hook, instead of leaving the agent to write its own loop.
- **Quota cockpit** (`quota`) — query `/apps/{token}/limits.json` so monitoring scripts can preflight before bursting.
- **Local redacted history ledger** — every send the CLI performs is written to a local SQLite ledger (token-redacted) for audit; `history search` does FTS5 across it.
- **Open Client inbox sync** (`inbox sync`) — download messages into local SQLite before optional delete-through, so an agent can read a snapshot without racing the live API.

author: cjimti
body:
## Summary

- **Audit detail panel** now shows request/response bodies as decoded JSON instead of base64 dumps. `Payload.MarshalJSON` emits utf-8 strings (with a `request_body_encoding`/`response_body_encoding=base64` flag fallback for non-utf-8 bytes so binary payloads still round-trip).
- **Try-It** returns 200 when a logged-in operator clicks Send instead of 401 "missing credential". The portal-resolved identity now bridges into the dispatched request's context; `httpmw.Identity` short-circuits when one is already set, except when a real credential is on the wire — so typing `X-API-Key: <other-key>` into the Try-It headers field to "test as a different principal" still resolves through the chain.
- **Audit replay** got the same identity bridge plus a filter that drops captured credential headers (`Authorization`, `X-API-Key`, `Cookie`) and the `api_key` query param before re-emission, since those values are persisted as the `[redacted]` sentinel and would otherwise look like wire credentials.

## Why the user ran into this

Both defects show up immediately on the live `api-test-server.plexara.io` deployment of v1.1.0 (audit panel showed base64 strings, Try-It returned 401 while the user was logged in via the portal session). The deployment manifest itself is correct; the defects are upstream in v1.1.0. Cutting a v1.1.1 tag here unblocks the cluster.

## Known limitation (deferred with TODO)

`hasInboundCredential` and `redactedReplayHeaders` hardcode the default api-key header/query names (`X-API-Key`, `api_key`). Deployments that customize `APIKeysConfig.HeaderName` / `QueryParamName` will silently lose Try-It "test as someone else" semantics under the custom name, and replay will leak the captured redaction sentinel for the custom header. The live deployment runs the defaults so this isn't a regression for the immediate rollout. Follow-up would either thread the configured names through `Identity()` or add a `HasCredential(r)` method to `inbound.Chain` that delegates to each authenticator.

## Test plan

- [x] `make verify` clean (fmt, vet, test, golangci-lint, gosec, semgrep, coverage gate, SPA-bundle in-sync check)
- [x] Unit tests: `Payload.MarshalJSON` (utf-8 / binary / empty); `httpmw.Identity` pre-set bypass + wire-cred override
- [x] Integration test: `TestAuditReplay_RedactedCredentialsThroughRealIdentityMW` mounts the real `httpmw.Identity` in front of the replay target with a chain that would reject `[redacted]`, asserts replay reaches the inner handler — would 401 if the redacted-header filter regressed
- [x] Local visual verify in browser via `make dev`: audit detail shows decoded JSON, Try-It on `/v1/whoami` returns 200 with `{"subject":"devkey","auth_type":"apikey","key_name":"devkey"}`
- [ ] Cut v1.1.1, redeploy to gpu1, confirm the live portal's audit detail and Try-It both render correctly

2. **Italian pass: A2-level + brand-aligned.** Revised the italian onboarding strings (tutorial cards, "best practices", three privacy variants) and the existing translated entries in `it-IT.po` against three rules:
   - A2 reading level (general public, basic italian)
   - Informal `tu`, never `Lei`/`voi`
   - Active voice over passive ("Cancelliamo i dati" not "I dati vengono cancellati")
   - Sentence case for titles
   - Lowercase `dembrane`, even at sentence start
   - Short sentences, no jargon

3. **Brand guide.** Added an `Italian localization` section to `brand/STYLE_GUIDE.md` mirroring the Dutch one — core rules, glossary, good/bad examples. Updated `AGENTS.md` to point at it. Added the italian A2 check to the pre-ship checklist.

## What changed

- `echo/frontend/src/components/participant/ParticipantOnboardingCards.tsx` — restore `it-IT` block (microphone-check + "tutto pronto" sections)
- `echo/frontend/src/components/participant/hooks/useOnboardingCards.ts` — pass over italian: basic tutorial cards, advanced tutorial cards, "best practices" section, three privacy variants (client-managed / consent / legitimate-interest)
- `echo/frontend/src/locales/it-IT.po` — fix `piu` → `più`, A2 polish on the 4 longer real translations
- `echo/frontend/src/locales/it-IT.ts` — regenerated via `pnpm messages:compile`
- `echo/brand/STYLE_GUIDE.md` — new `Italian localization` section + checklist item
- `echo/AGENTS.md` — pointer to the italian section

## Cross-check

- it-IT pilot URL fixed locally: `pnpm messages:compile` → onboarding cards now render in italian on `portal.dembrane.com/it-IT/...`
- `pnpm exec biome check` clean on touched files
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` clean
- No changes to en-US / nl-NL / de-DE / fr-FR / es-ES / uk-UA strings — only the `it-IT.ts` compiled output

## What I didn't touch

- `it-IT.po` still has ~880 untranslated entries (en-US placeholders) and ~378 empty. Pauline's brief was "first information slides and portal instructions" — i scoped this PR to the onboarding cards + the already-translated entries. The remaining bulk-translation of the `.po` is a separate question (sameer to confirm scope).
- `uk-UA` onboarding cards block left on en-US fallback per instructions.
- `echo-user-docs` site — no italian content there. Same scoping question.
- Native-italian review pass — flagged on the stakeholder side; this PR is model-grade italian against the A2 + brand rules. Worth a native review before going live for ActionAid.

## Confidence

Medium. The bug fix part is mechanical and well-isolated (one file, additive, matches the pattern of the other locales). The translation pass is where the uncertainty sits: i can produce italian that reads naturally and follows the A2 + brand rules, but i'm not a native speaker — a native reviewer should sanity-check tone before this ships to the ActionAid pilot. Specific spots i'd flag for review:

- privacy variant 3 (legitimate-interest): the GDPR phrasing has to stay legally accurate while being A2
- consent checkbox label: changed `"Acconsento alla registrazione e al trattamento..."` → `"Accetto che la mia conversazione sia registrata e trattata."` — clearer but still affirmative

- **Stats row** — two bento tiles side-by-side: `Currently present` driven by the existing `LiveCounter` flip animation (green), and an inferred `Absent / not-yet-scanned` count over the expected total (red). Each shows `value / total` with tabular figures.
- **Segmented pill tabs** — replaced the underline `TabBar` with a rounded pill segmented control (red pill on white surface, soft tile shadow).
- **Entry list** — each row is a bento mini-card with a gold-on-navy initials avatar, name + ID, and the existing `StatusChip` for tone. Slide-in + fade animations preserved.
- **Sticky bottom action bar** — separated from scroll, soft top shadow, full-width red "End lecture" CTA at 52px height. Calls the same end logic as the back arrow.

### i18n

Added 8 new `doctor.*` keys in both English and Arabic dictionaries (`welcome`, `welcomeFallback`, `lectureStartsIn`, `scanPrompt`, `rotatesIn`, `expectedLabel`, `backToToday`, `todayLabel`). Updated `qr_display.dart` so the "Rotates in {seconds}s" pill reads from `doctor.rotatesIn` instead of being hardcoded in English.

### Not changed

- Routing, role guards, `authProvider`, and `/me/schedule/today` contract are untouched.
- Backend / admin / test scaffolding untouched.
- PR #9 (the login redirect fix) is separate and already merged-ready — this PR is purely UI.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Pull the branch and run the Flutter web build (or your usual device target) and confirm the doctor home renders the new bento layout — countdown hero, stats row, lecture cards with accent bars.
- [ ] Verify "Start lecture" (from the hero, from a lecture card, or by tapping the card body) still routes to `/doctor/active` with the correct subject / section / room / slotId payload.
- [ ] Confirm the active-session screen renders correctly on your shortest phone — the QR + stats + tabs + entry list should all be visible above the sticky "End lecture" bar without overflow.
- [ ] Swap to Arabic from the profile screen and confirm both screens flip cleanly (header icons mirror, pulse chip + buttons still readable). Specifically check the active-session back arrow direction.
- [ ] Pause through a full QR rotation on the active screen and confirm the "Rotates in Xs" pill counts down and the countdown ring tracks it.

### Notes

- The doctor `_TodaySlot` gained optional `startTime` / `endTime` HH:mm fields (parsed off the existing `/me/schedule/today` payload). The fallback `time` rendered string is unchanged for callers that only set `startTime` / `endTime` strings.
- Mobile `flutter analyze` on the touched files reports clean; the remaining repo-wide info-level lints (`app_theme.dart`, `attendance_ring.dart`, `widget_test.dart`) are pre-existing and unrelated to this PR — they also exist on `main` and CI was green there.

body:
## 1. What changed and why

Fourth slice of the rag_core decomposition series (PR-H1a/b → PR-J1 → PR-J2 → this PR). With this slice landing, the series completes the major decomposition: rag_core drops from 4,201 LOC to 2,843 LOC (-32% total), and four cohesive modules (\`rag_retrieval\`, \`rag_verifier\`, \`rag_answer\`, \`rag_query\`) own their respective responsibilities.

Moves 15 functions from \`rag_core.py:1318-1796\` (~479 LOC) to new \`rag_query.py\`:
- Query inspection: \`is_metadata_ambiguous\`, \`has_implicit_reference\`, \`has_comparison_request\`, \`extract_requested_agencies\`
- Conversation state helpers: \`active_state_terms\`, \`active_state_size\`, \`inject_entities_into_query\`, \`make_context_resolution\`
- Main entries: \`resolve_conversation_context\`, \`analyze_query\`
- Metadata helpers: \`comparison_targets_for_analysis\`, \`summarize_metadata_match\`, \`metadata_resolution_diagnostics\`
- Planner: \`query_type_default_top_k\`, \`make_plan\`

Closes #478

## 2. Files affected

- \`rag_query.py\` (new) — 597 LOC (the 479-line block + 60-line module docstring + imports + late-import statements)
- \`rag_core.py\` — delete lines 1318-1796, add re-export
- \`CLAUDE.md\`, \`scripts/_governance.py\`, \`.github/pull_request_template.md\` — repository map / load-bearing list / PR-template hint updates

Load-bearing per \`scripts/_governance.py\`: \`rag_core.py\`, new \`rag_query.py\`.

## 3. Risks

Highest-likelihood break (and the one I hit twice during impl): missing late-imports for rag_core utilities. Caught in local pytest:
- \`metadata_filters_from_matches\` (used inside \`analyze_query\`)
- \`QUERY_TYPE_TOP_K_DEFAULTS\` (used inside \`make_plan\`)

After both fixes, the full pytest run is clean (\`838 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed\`).

Second risk: cross-module impact via \`comparison_targets_for_analysis\` which is late-imported by \`rag_retrieval\` and \`rag_answer\`. Mitigation — \`rag_core\` re-exports the moved name, so \`from rag_core import comparison_targets_for_analysis\` keeps working. No \`rag_retrieval\` / \`rag_answer\` changes needed.

Third risk: behavior drift. Mechanical move + late-imports. Every line preserved verbatim.

## 4. Tests

No new tests. Five existing regression gates:
- \`tests/test_naive_baseline_ranking_invariance.py\` (ADR 0001 golden)
- \`tests/test_retrieval_loop_regression.py\`
- \`tests/test_langgraph_orchestrator_regression.py\` (JSON-identity)
- \`tests/test_conversation_state_*.py\` (context resolution surface)
- \`tests/test_governance.py\` (49 cases)

## 5. Eval impact

All \`·\`. 15 functions move bit-for-bit.

### 5b. Real-data delta

No behavior change in retrieval / verifier path. Mechanical move + late-imports for circular-avoidance; every line preserved verbatim. \`naive_baseline\` golden bit-identical.

## 6. Backward compatibility

\`rag_core\` re-exports all 15 public names so any caller importing them (orchestration \`_phase_analyze\`, tests, scripts, \`rag_retrieval\` / \`rag_answer\` late-imports of \`comparison_targets_for_analysis\`) keeps working unchanged. No CLI flags / schema / contract changes.

## 7. Out of scope

The remaining bulk in \`rag_core.py\` (~2,843 LOC after this PR) is mostly orchestration core (\`_RunContext\`, three phase functions, \`run_rag_query\`), clarification result building, chunking / index preparation, and metadata matching utilities. Further extraction is possible (clarification path ~277 LOC was the next candidate per the original Explore analysis) but the user requested PR-J2 + PR-J3 only for this round.

| PR | Module | LOC moved | rag_core after |
|---|---|---|---|
| #460 (PR-H1a) | rag_retrieval (apply_fusion + helpers) | ~210 | 3,990 |
| #462 (PR-H1b) | rag_retrieval (retrieve_candidates + BM25) | ~390 | 3,635 |
| #466 (PR-J1) | rag_verifier | ~203 | 3,635 → after offset shift |
| #474 (PR-J2) | rag_answer | ~362 | 3,300 |
| #478 (this PR) | rag_query | ~457 | **2,843** |

author: zackees
body:
## Summary

Fixes the long-running CI smoke-test failure visible on every recent main run (e.g. https://github.com/zackees/soldr/actions/runs/25766573648/job/75680494573 — Linux x64, with identical Windows x64 and macOS x64 failures).

## Root cause

CI's setup-soldr action exports `SOLDR_TARGET_CACHE_MODE=full` and `SOLDR_BUILD_CACHE_MODE=full` into the job environment. Seven CLI smoke tests spawn soldr with a fake cargo binary (`SOLDR_TEST_CARGO_BIN`). The spawned soldr inherits the cache-mode env vars, triggers the rust-plan path, runs `cargo metadata` against the fake (which returns `{}`), and panics:

```
soldr: failed to parse cargo metadata while preparing Rust artifact cache plan: missing field `packages` at line 1 column 2
```

Predates this branch — verified the same 7 failures on the 0.7.16 release commit (#271, run 25703498029). Local devs don't see it because no shell exports those env vars at the workstation level.

## Fix

Strip both env vars at the spawn site of every fake-toolchain test:

- `cargo_front_door_uses_soldr_wrapper_and_managed_zccache_by_default`
- `cargo_front_door_recovers_from_stale_zccache_daemon_start`
- `cargo_front_door_uses_real_tool_overrides_before_path_probe`
- `cargo_front_door_detects_build_after_global_cargo_options`
- `cargo_front_door_preserves_jobserver_fds_into_managed_zccache_wrapper`
- `cache_enabled_zccache_build_completes_under_20_seconds`
- `nested_soldr_ignores_inherited_managed_zccache_cache_dir`

One-line `.env_remove("SOLDR_TARGET_CACHE_MODE")` + `.env_remove("SOLDR_BUILD_CACHE_MODE")` per spawn chain. A short comment at the first occurrence documents the rationale so future fake-toolchain tests follow the same pattern.

Why test-side instead of soldr-side: the fake-cargo `{}` metadata response is a test artifact; it shouldn't dictate soldr CLI behavior. soldr's metadata parsing is correct — the tests just need to opt out of triggering it.

## Test plan

- [x] Reproduce failure locally: `SOLDR_TARGET_CACHE_MODE=full cargo test -p soldr-cli --test cli cache_enabled_zccache_build_completes_under_20_seconds` — fails identically to CI
- [x] Apply fix, rerun under `SOLDR_TARGET_CACHE_MODE=full SOLDR_BUILD_CACHE_MODE=full` — all 6 Windows-visible tests pass
- [x] 7th test (`cargo_front_door_preserves_jobserver_fds...`) is `#[cfg(not(windows))]`; got the same edit so it lands cleanly on Linux/macOS CI
- [x] `cargo test -p soldr-cli` — 72 + 36 + 3 = 111 tests pass
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean
- [ ] On merge: Linux x64 / macOS x64 / Windows x64 CI jobs flip from failure to success

author: jeffhurst
body:
### Motivation
- Observations could contain planet records as dicts or attribute objects, but metrics parsed raw rows positionally which caused exceptions when diagnostic collection ran before returning the observation.  
- Candidate feature vectors were generated in `generate_candidates` but never appended to the fixed-size observation, so the policy did not receive explicit per-candidate information.  
- Target-owner metrics relied on a `purpose` field that candidates did not include, producing useless zeroed metrics in TensorBoard.

### Description
- Reworked metrics to use the defensive observation parsing helpers from `observation_encoder` by calling `get_planets` and `get_player` so `summarize_planets`, `count_captures_and_losses`, and related helpers accept dict and attribute-style planet rows (changes in `src/orbit_wars_rl/features/metrics.py`).
- Added `purpose` and `target_owner` to `send` candidates in `generate_candidates` and populated them as `capture_neutral`, `attack_enemy`, or `reinforce` based on the target owner (changes in `src/orbit_wars_rl/features/candidate_generator.py`).
- Introduced `CANDIDATE_FEATURES`, a `_candidate_features` helper, and updated `encode_observation` to accept a `candidates` list and `max_candidates`, append padded/truncated candidate feature rows to the encoded vector, and updated `observation_size` accordingly (changes in `src/orbit_wars_rl/features/observation_encoder.py`).
- Updated the Gym wrapper to size the observation space for candidate-aware observations and to pass the current candidate list into `encode_observation` at reset and step (changes in `src/orbit_wars_rl/envs/orbit_wars_gym.py`).
- Updated the Kaggle submission agent to pass generated candidates into `encode_observation` for inference so the model sees the new observation layout (changes in `src/orbit_wars_rl/submit_agent.py`).
- Added and adjusted unit tests: `tests/test_metrics.py` (new), updated `tests/test_observation_encoder.py` to assert candidate feature encoding and object-observation support, and extended `tests/test_candidate_generator.py` to validate `target_owner` and `purpose` metadata.

### Testing
- Ran `python -m compileall -q src tests` which succeeded without syntax errors.  
- Ran code formatting with `black` which completed and reformatted files as expected.  
- Executed `pytest -q`, which attempted to run the unit tests but collection failed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'numpy'` because runtime/test dependencies are not available in this environment, so unit tests could not be executed here.  
- Attempted `python -m pip install -e '.[dev]'` and `pyright` in this environment, but both could not install/resolve runtime dependencies (network/build restrictions and missing packages), so full CI-style validation was not possible in this runner.
